commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MLA] Scope DSpark non-causal capability to builder layers
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

`MLAAttentionSpec.merge` unions `non_causal_multi_token_decode` across every layer in a KV cache group. After #55234 a causal target and a DSpark draft can share that group, so the target's metadata builder inherited the draft flag and failed DCP validation even though it only served causal layers.

Resolve the flag from the builder's own layers in `static_forward_context`. Do not fall back to the merged group spec: that is the value that incorrectly marked the target as non-causal.

Command used that fails:
```
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
    --served-model-name kimi-k3 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
   --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
   --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
    --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \
    --max-model-len 135168 \
    --max-num-seqs 8 \
    --max_num_batched_tokens 4096 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --quantization-config '{"moe":{"weight":"int4_per_group_32"}}' \
    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "model": "Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "attention
_backend": "TRITON_MLA", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "block"}' \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000
```

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_noncausal.py -q`
- [x] Kimi-K3 + DSpark + DCP with AITER target / Triton draft boots past `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder does not support non-causal draft...`

Depends on #54546 for the Triton draft path under DCP to have DSpark + DCP fully functional on gfx942. However, this PR can be merged independently.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Re-enable the DSv4.1 decoder replay graph test on ROCm
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

`tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py::test_replay_graph_matches_eager` was skipped on ROCm in #60378 because it fails there. The failure is a detail of the test setup, not a platform limitation, so this restores the test and fixes the setup instead.

## History

- #59532 added the test together with `DecoderReplayCudaGraphManager`.
- #60378 skipped it on ROCm with the reason "decoder replay CUDA graphs are NVIDIA-only".

## Problem

The test builds its config as a `MagicMock`, so every attribute lookup returns a truthy mock, including `use_cumem_cudagraph_pool`. Graph capture is therefore routed into the cuMem pool. On ROCm the cuMem mapping zeroes freshly remapped VRAM with a `hipMemset` on the legacy default stream (`csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp`), which HIP refuses while a capture is in flight:

```
operation would make the legacy stream depend on a capturing blocking stream
```

The capture is invalidated and the test fails.

The real property ends with `and current_platform.is_cuda()`, so this path is unreachable on ROCm outside the test. There is no production issue here.

## Fix

Set `cfg.use_cumem_cudagraph_pool = False` on the mock, which keeps the capture in the regular pool, and drop the ROCm skip.

## Validation

The whole file on an AMD GPU:

```
3 passed in 4.19s
```

I also ran the full `Basic Models (Other)` group locally and it is passed.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend][Rust] Add gRPC forbidden token sequences and cache usage
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add forbidden token sequences and cached-token usage to the Rust gRPC API. This extends the existing typed protobuf fields and shared text lowering.

## Claims

- Accept `DecodingParameters.bad_words_token_ids`, such as `[[7, 11]]`, and forward exact token sequences to engine-core alongside any text-layer `bad_words`; reject empty or out-of-vocabulary sequences.
- Return `FinishInfo.num_cached_tokens` on terminal unary and streaming responses, including explicit zero. An absent count distinguishes servers that do not report this value.

## Validation

From `rust/`:

```sh
cargo test --locked -p vllm-server -p vllm-text --lib -- --quiet
```

437 server tests and 103 text tests passed; one existing text test is ignored. Scoped pre-commit checks passed.

The request boundary regression exercises protobuf serialization and lowering of forbidden token sequences into engine-core parameters. Text-layer coverage checks raw/string bad-word merging and invalid sequences. Response checks cover nonzero cached usage through protobuf conversion and explicit zero through both real gRPC handlers with a mock engine-core.

No real-model/GPU validation has been performed; this is a draft pending that validation and human review.

## Details

The gRPC schema lacks these fields, while engine-core already supports forbidden token sequences and the text layer already accumulates cached-token usage. This change carries those existing values through the typed API. The protobuf additions use new field numbers; older servers ignore the new request fields. Adding generated Rust struct fields affects source compatibility; the crate version bump is deferred to a separate PR.

Explicit zero/false preservation is handled separately in #60115, and reasoning controls in #59836. These PRs target `main` independently. Related #56776 proposes a separate native-sampling JSON payload; this PR extends the existing typed API and adds shared text support for pre-tokenized forbidden sequences.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Add AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill backend
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Add `aiter_flydsl` as an opt-in GDN prefill backend on ROCm. Supported BF16 GDN layers with 128-dimensional key and value heads route through AITER's optimized VK implementation with both the fused FlyDSL prepare stage and FlyDSL K5 enabled; unsupported platforms, shapes, dtypes, and older AITER builds retain the Triton/FLA path.

This requires the AITER APIs from ROCm/aiter#4532, ROCm/aiter#4598, ROCm/aiter#4694, ROCm/aiter#4732, and the prepare-kernel fix in ROCm/aiter#4952; all merged.

## Test Plan

**Hardware:** 8x MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3
**Model:** `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8, BF16 GDN, FP8 KV cache

* **Kernel case:** Added `test_aiter_flydsl_prefill_matches_triton_reference`: packed sequences `[70, 130]`, BF16 Q/K/V, FP32 state, 128-dim heads, GQA ratio 2, run on device and compared against the *same* AITER entry point with `use_chunk_flydsl`/`use_prepare_flydsl` off. Using that as the reference means the two calls differ only in the kernels this backend exists to select. Verified passing on MI355X (gfx950).
* **Reference:** AITER `chunk_gated_delta_rule_opt_vk` with Triton prepare and Triton VK K5
* **Unit tests:** `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py`, pruned to the cases that guard correctness:
  * `test_aiter_flydsl_prefill_matches_triton_reference[fp32_state|bf16_state]` — the numerical check. Packed sequences `[70, 130]` (both span several 64-token chunks and end in a partial one), BF16 Q/K/V, 128-dim heads, GQA ratio 2, run on device against the *same* AITER entry point with `use_chunk_flydsl`/`use_prepare_flydsl` off, so the two calls differ only in the kernels this backend selects. Parametrized over the SSM state dtype because `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` can make it FP32 or BF16 and the backend forwards `initial_state.dtype` to AITER; it also asserts the final state comes back in that dtype, since it is written back into the cache.
  * `test_resolve_aiter_flydsl_gdn_prefill_backend` — the shape/dtype gate. FlyDSL is only taken for BF16 with 128/128 key/value heads; any other combination must stay on Triton rather than reach kernels that don't support it.
  * `test_kda_style_model_cannot_select_flydsl` — Kimi K3 KDA shares this layer but builds its own chunk metadata, which the FlyDSL path skips. This pins that the resolver turns it down before that mismatch can happen.
  * `test_explicit_aiter_flydsl_fails_closed[kernels_missing|not_rocm]` — an explicit `aiter_flydsl` request on a build without the kernels, or off ROCm, raises instead of silently running Triton and reporting the run as FlyDSL.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model Loader] Support reload_weights with runai_streamer load format
commits.pr_body:
### Purpose

`GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` reloads weights from the checkpoint source through the configured model loader's `get_all_weights()`. Only `DefaultModelLoader` implements it. With `--load-format runai_streamer`, the documented sleep level 2 flow in `docs/features/sleep_mode.md`

```python
llm.sleep(level=2)                    # discard weights and KV cache, no host backup
llm.wake_up(tags=["weights"])
llm.collective_rpc("reload_weights")  # fails
llm.wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])
```

fails at the reload step with `NotImplementedError: Model reloading with runai_streamer format`.

`reload_weights` originally called the loader's `load_weights()` (#20096), which every loader has. #32133 switched it to `get_all_weights()` so the runner can wrap `model.load_weights()` in the layerwise reload, gated on `hasattr(model_loader, "get_all_weights")`, and left `# TODO(@kylesayrs): generalize to all runners and loaders`. This PR is the loader half of that TODO for `runai_streamer`.

### Consequences

Sleep level 2 is unusable for engines started with the streamer. Level 1 works but keeps a full host-RAM copy of the weights, which is what level 2 exists to avoid. There is no supported way to load with the streamer and reload with the default loader. Checkpoints served from object storage (`s3://`, `gs://`, Azure Blob) cannot be reloaded at all: `VllmConfig.__post_init__` resolves `load_format=auto` to `runai_streamer` for these URIs and rejects other formats, so every object-storage user is affected, not only those who chose the streamer.

### Solution

**Loader.** Add `get_all_weights()` to `RunaiModelStreamerLoader`. It resolves the same source as `load_weights()` (`model_weights` when set, otherwise `model`, with `revision` passed through), and `load_weights()` now consumes it so the two paths cannot diverge. `reload_weights` then streams the checkpoint from local FS, NFS or object storage exactly as the initial load did.

**Runner.** Making the streamer reachable from `reload_weights` exposed a second gap, specific to object storage plus `weights_path`. `ModelConfig` keeps an object-storage model in two fields: `model_weights` holds the URI and `model` points at the temp directory of pulled config files. `reload_weights(weights_path=...)` rewrote `model` and reset `revision` but never touched `model_weights`, so the loader kept preferring the stale URI and silently re-streamed the original bucket. One line in `gpu_model_runner.py` clears `model_weights` in the same block that resets `revision`, for the same reason: both belong to the model being reloaded away from. `DefaultModelLoader` never reads the field, and a bare `reload_weights()` leaves both fields alone and still reloads the original bucket.

### Testing

All runs on an NVIDIA H200 NVL with `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0`, the loader and runner changes applied in place, each test run on the stock code first and then on the patched code.

| Test | Job | Stock | Patched |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_runai_get_all_weights_resolves_source[object_storage\|hf_repo]` (CPU, mocked iterator) | Model Executor | `AttributeError: no attribute 'get_all_weights'` | 2 passed |
| `test_runai_deep_sleep_reload_weights` (GPU) | Model Executor | `NotImplementedError` at the first reload | passed, whole directory 18 passed, 1 skipped |
| `test_runai_reload_weights_path_from_mocked_s3` (GPU, `StreamerPatcher`, no real S3) | Model Executor | fails at the `weights_path` step, parameter unchanged (relative diff 0.50) | 2 passed |
| `test_reload_weights_path_replaces_object_storage_source` (CPU, `Mock`) | v1/worker | `'s3://bucket/original' != ''` | passed |

- `test_runai_get_all_weights_resolves_source`: `get_all_weights` prefers `model_weights` when set, falls back to `model` when empty, and forwards `revision`.
- `test_runai_deep_sleep_reload_weights`: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B with sleep mode on, three cycles of `sleep(level=2)` → `wake_up(["weights"])` → `reload_weights(weights_path=...)` → `wake_up(["kv_cache"])`: the multiply and add debug checkpoints must flip the perplexity ordering, and reloading the base checkpoint must reproduce the pre-sleep output byte for byte. GPU usage is bounded after each sleep and each reload step, mirroring `test_deep_sleep`. Not fork-isolated on purpose: in the Model Executor session CUDA is already initialised in the pytest process, and a forked child that touches CUDA fails with "Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess" (reproduced).
- `test_runai_reload_weights_path_from_mocked_s3`: engine started from `s3://my-mock-bucket/gpt2/` served from `tmp_path`, like the existing mocked-S3 test. A bare `reload_weights()` must re-stream the original bucket (tensor zeroed first), `reload_weights(weights_path="s3://my-mock-bucket/gpt2-mod/")` must load the second checkpoint (`ln_f.weight` scaled by 2), and a bare reload afterwards must reload the second checkpoint.
- `test_reload_weights_path_replaces_object_storage_source`: the runner hands the loader `(model=weights_path, model_weights="", revision=None)`. Kept alongside the integration test because the Model Executor job is not triggered by changes under `vllm/v1/worker`; this one runs in the v1/worker job.

End to end on the same H200 with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct` (BF16, 8 shards, 27.5 GiB): `sleep(level=2)`, `wake_up(["weights"])`, `collective_rpc("reload_weights")`, `wake_up(["kv_cache"])`, outputs byte-identical to pre-sleep over 20 cycles, `CuMemAllocator` confirming `0.00 GiB is backed up in CPU`. Against MinIO on the node, across two buckets: an engine started from `s3://vllm-models/qwen3-0.6b/` kept serving the original weights after `reload_weights(weights_path="s3://vllm-models-b/…")` on the stock runner, and matched an HF-started reference with the runner change; a bare `reload_weights()` reloaded the original bucket before the override and the new bucket after it, and the target prefixes held only `model.safetensors`.

### Performance Results

**Local XFS (virtio disk), cold reload after `sleep(level=2)`:**
- runai_streamer (this PR): 23.9 s, 22.4 s
- default loader, default heuristic (no prefetch on local FS): 112.7 s, 112.4 s
- default loader, `--safetensors-load-strategy prefetch`: 26.9 s, 26.7 s

**NFSv4.1, cold reload:**
- runai_streamer, default settings: 113.9 s, 98.8 s
- runai_streamer, `RUNAI_STREAMER_CONCURRENCY=8`, 8 MiB chunks: 89.3 s, 82.2 s
- default loader: 89.0 s, 63.3 s

**Object storage (MinIO on the node):** stock v0.29.0 fails at reload with `NotImplementedError` for both `--load-format runai_streamer` and `auto`; this PR reloads in 31.7 s and 30.6 s with identical outputs.

### Documentation

`docs/features/sleep_mode.md` already describes the level 2 + `reload_weights` flow; no change needed.

### AI Disclosure

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). All lines were reviewed by the submitter; the end-to-end runs above were executed and checked manually.

## Purpose

Before this change, `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` routed a decode GEMM to the HIP `wvSplitK_int4_g` kernel only when the activation row count was at most five (`M <= 5`) and the total activation size satisfied `K * M <= 32768`.

The existing C++ operator supports up to five activation rows (`N_in <= 5`) and accepts `K_in * N_in` up to `int(max_lds_len * 1.2)`. With `max_lds_len = 32768`, the effective upper limit is `39321` elements.

Python `M` maps to C++ `N_in`. For inputs above the regular LDS capacity, the medium kernel keeps the activation prefix in LDS and reads the remaining elements from global memory.

Consequently, supported shapes with `K * M` between `32768` and `39321` (exclusive of the lower bound and inclusive of the upper bound) fell back to Triton instead of using the existing HIP kernel.

This PR aligns the Python dispatch limit with the C++ operator contract. It also adds dispatch-boundary tests and numerical correctness coverage for the newly enabled range. No C++ kernel is changed.

## Duplicate-work check

Open PR searches for medium-skinny, wvSplitK W4A16, and RDNA hybrid W4A16 found no duplicate. Related PRs #46186, #51511, and #50618 do not modify this hybrid dispatch threshold.

## Test Plan

Test environment:

All tests were run locally on the following system:

| --- | --- |
| GPU | AMD Radeon 8060S |
| GPU architecture | gfx1151 |
| Memory | 128 GB unified memory (96 GiB VRAM, 32 GiB host-visible) |
| Operating system | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS |
| ROCm | 7.2.3 |

The end-to-end comparison covered the two medium-skinny `down_proj` shapes below:

| `Qwen3-4B-GPTQ-Int4` | 4 | `M=4, K=9728, N=2560` | 38912 | Triton | HIP medium |

- `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` with the `ROCM_ATTN` backend;

Functional validation included dispatch tests at the regular and medium boundaries, FP16 and BF16 medium-kernel comparisons against an FP32 reference, and the complete hybrid W4A16 test file. All applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` were also run on the changed files.

## Purpose

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` is silently ignored for GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`): `Glm5NextMoE` builds `FusedMoE` with `n_shared_experts=None`, so each of the 42 MoE layers still runs the shared expert as a separate MLP (two FP8 block-scale GEMMs, a clamped SiLU and a quant) and adds it to the routed output.

This PR wires the flag up the way `DeepseekV2MoE` does:

- **MoE:** when `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert()` allows it, `Glm5NextMoE` drops the separate MLP and passes `n_shared_experts` / `fuse_shared_experts` to `FusedMoE`, so the shared expert runs as one more expert inside the AITER fused MoE (`E=289, topk=9`). The routed weights keep `routed_scaling_factor` and the shared slot gets 1.0, so the output is the same `shared + routed` sum as before.
- **Loading:** in both the target and the MTP draft model, the checkpoint's `mlp.shared_experts.*` tensors (FP8 scales included) load into expert slot `n_routed_experts`. `is_model_fused_shared_expert_compatible()` keeps fusion all-or-nothing, and more than one shared expert raises.
- **Gate:** AITER has tuned configs for the fused shape only on gfx950 at TP4 and TP8 (ROCm/aiter#5735, shipped in AITER v0.1.23, already in vLLM's ROCm image since #58867). Like DeepSeek-V4's shared-expert gate, `_fused_shared_experts_tuned()` allows fusion only there, and only without data, prefill context or expert parallelism, which change the per-rank shape. Anywhere else the flag logs a one-time warning with the reason, and the shared experts stay a separate MLP.

Nothing changes unless the flag is set on gfx950 at TP4 or TP8: it defaults to off, and `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert()` returns False on non-ROCm platforms. gfx942 will follow in a separate PR once its rows (ROCm/aiter#5953) ship; without them the fused MoE would run untuned kernels (4289 µs vs 3033 µs for one 16K-token MoE call on MI325X).

## Test Plan

gfx950 (MI350X), `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` FP8, on the stock ROCm nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-0cbac6cd1305f710e12193596b27488397bcb205` (AITER v0.1.23) with no patches besides this PR. VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code \
  --compilation-config '{"custom_ops": ["all"]}'

for c in 2 4 6 8 10 12 16; do
  vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 \
    --random-output-len 1024 --num-prompts 20 --num-warmups 2 --max-concurrency $c
done

# lm_eval 0.4.13, all 1319 questions
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,timeout=3600,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn \

pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py

The gate runs and unit tests ran at [3c2d001](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/3c2d001f37069274f941d8fe4a95e2ff6c5c79e8), which has the same three files as the current head (18fa78d).

## Test Result

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Derive the QSA head_dim from the unsharded head count
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Qwen4Exp QSA computes its fallback `head_dim` from `num_heads`, which is already divided by the tensor-parallel size, so on TP > 1 the fallback is `tp_size` times too large. The fallback is latent: `Qwen4ExpTextConfig` defaults `head_dim` to 256 and rejects `None`, so only an explicit `head_dim: 0` reaches it. This fixes the arithmetic so it matches the `hidden_size // total_num_heads` idiom used elsewhere.

## Claims

- The fallback divides by the unsharded head count, so it is correct on any TP size.
- No change for any config with a nonzero `head_dim`, which covers every real checkpoint.

## Validation

```
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/
```

Unchanged against `main` on compute capability 8.0: this is reached only when `config.head_dim` is 0, which no Qwen3.8-Flash-Next config sets, so no existing test exercises the fallback.

The defect is by inspection of the surrounding lines:

```python
self.total_num_heads = int(config.num_attention_heads)
...
self.num_heads = self.total_num_heads // tp_size
...
self.head_dim = int(config.head_dim or self.hidden_size // self.num_heads)
```

`hidden_size` is sized against the unsharded head count, so dividing by the sharded one overstates `head_dim` by exactly `tp_size`. `q_size` and `kv_size` are then built from it, so the QKV projection is created at the wrong width and the checkpoint fails to load with a shape mismatch rather than producing wrong output.

No test added: the fallback has no checkpoint behind it in the suite, and a test would have to fabricate a config with `head_dim: 0` purely to assert one arithmetic expression. The failure mode is a loud shape mismatch, not a silent wrong result.

Not validated end to end: no real checkpoint reaches the fallback.

## Details

The same expression appears on the CUDA and ROCm QSA owners and both are changed. `total_num_heads` is assigned a few lines above the fallback in each, so no reordering is needed.

## Overview

Guard the three `EmbeddingGemma2` pooling tests that require `transformers >= 5.19.0`, which currently fail the `Multimodal Models (Extended Pooling)` group on both NVIDIA and AMD. Follow-up to #60254 and #60295.

## Claims

- Fixes `test_encoder_contract`, `test_video_loader_indices` and `test_video_loader_duplicate_expansion`, which fail with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'transformers.models.embedding_gemma2'`.
- Applies to both `(H200 MIG 18GB)` and `(MI300)`, since both install the pinned `transformers==5.18.0`.
- Changes no version pin and no production code; test-only.
- The two tests in the file that do not need the new module keep running.

Failure in CI: [CI #93244](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93244/list?sid=01a114f8-863b-4842-a77e-2d9683c590c9&tab=output)

|---|---|
| before | 3 failed, 2 passed, 15 skipped |
| after | 2 passed, 18 skipped |

With `transformers 5.19.0` installed the three tests run and pass, confirming the tests are correct and only the pin blocks them.

## Details

#60254 added the model and these tests. They import `transformers.models.embedding_gemma2`, which first ships in transformers 5.19.0, but `requirements/common.txt` caps `< 5.19.0` and the test requirements pin `5.18.0`; the PR changed no requirements file. #60295 fixed the same root cause for the registry test by raising `min_transformers_version` to `5.19.0`. This PR applies that same mechanism to the pooling tests, which it did not cover because they live in a different file. Reusing `HF_EXAMPLE_MODELS` keeps the required version declared in only one place. The guard is a per-test fixture rather than `autouse` so the unaffected tests still run, and it resolves itself once transformers is bumped, whether the registry entry is kept or removed.

commits.pr_title: [Misc] Report a missing DeepSelect extension only when it is requested
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`indexer_topk.py` warns at import whenever `vllm._deepselect_C` is missing, which is every build outside the SM100 family, and an explicit `deep_select` top-k request on an SM10x build without the extension fails with an `AttributeError`. The import now only records whether it succeeded, and the request reports the missing extension instead.

## Claims

- No `Failed to import the DeepSelect extension` warning at startup on builds that do not ship DeepSelect, whatever the model.
- An explicit `deep_select` request on SM10x without the extension fails with `vllm._deepselect_C could not be imported` instead of an `AttributeError` from `torch.ops.deep_select`.
- The import queries no device, and selection is unchanged otherwise; DeepSelect stays opt-in, so outputs are not affected.

## Validation

On main (`6ad2e06c4a`) with and without this commit, on an sm_80 machine without the extension: import `vllm.model_executor.layers.indexer_topk` and call `SparseIndexerTopk(backend="deep_select").resolve_backend(...)`, as is and with `is_device_capability_family` patched to report the SM100 family.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| warning at import | yes | no |
| capability queries during import | 0 | 0 |
| `deep_select` on sm_80 | `requires SM100a/SM103a (10.x device family)` | same |
| `deep_select` on SM100 (patched), extension missing | `AttributeError: '_OpNamespace' 'deep_select' object has no attribute 'get_alignment_requirement'` | `RuntimeError: ... vllm._deepselect_C could not be imported` |

## Details

The extension is only built for the SM100 family (`cmake/external_projects/deepselect.cmake`), and the module is imported while the engine config is built, so the warning reached every startup elsewhere. It came with #56464. Logging only on SM10x at import would need a capability query there, which initializes CUDA on platforms without NVML, so the diagnostic moves to `resolve_backend`, the only place a user asks for DeepSelect, as one more failure reason after the existing SM10x check. The DSA sparse-logits path already checks the extension through `has_deep_select()` and is unchanged.

No open PR addresses this: searches for the DeepSelect import and its warning return nothing related.

## Overview

Synchronous MoRIIO RDMA READs can race GPU zeroing of recycled attention pages in hybrid models. Exclude this step's aligned READ destinations in `build_connector_meta()` and explicitly document the limited zeroing-list exception to that hook's read-only contract.

This fix was extracted from #58968. It complements #59504's asynchronous-load handling; neither contains this synchronous MoRIIO protection.

## Claims

- Only fully overwritten hybrid READ attention destinations skip zeroing. Local compute tails, recurrent-state/scratch pages, other requests' pages and later reuse retain zeroing.
- Check READ mode, hybrid state and a nonempty zeroing list once, outside the request loop. No new synchronization or metadata format.
- The base hook permits removal only from `new_block_ids_to_zero`, with completion-before-use and fail-on-load-error obligations. Every other output field remains read-only; scheduler/cache-manager/model-runner/MultiConnector runtime code is unchanged.
- Reuse `test_update_state_drops_decode_recompute_tail_block` and its helpers. Remove the duplicate test from `test_moriio_tp_ack.py` and the obsolete ROCm/MoRI skip around the CPU scheduler suite.

## Validation

**Review revision `a1aef7fe3`:** 16 parameterized boundary cases pass, including no external attention hit, attention-only loads, empty zeroing lists, local tails, other output fields and next-step reuse. The same cases pass against the previous PR method; substituting the unmodified main method produces the expected **2 failed / 14 passed**. Connector regressions: **216 passed / 4 deselected**. Core regression selection: **47 passed / 369 deselected**. Selections overlap. Changed-file pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy pass. Four local checks using the real MultiConnector allocation/metadata methods also pass, covering MoRIIO in either position and selected/unselected ownership.

**Completed model evaluation:** [run 37203257111](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/37203257111), integration `34735d677`, achieved **1268/1319 (96.1334%)** for both flexible extract and strict match. This evaluated the previous connector-local implementation (`08469e5c9`) before this minor refactor and documentation update, plus the K3 MLA grouping, atomic TCP-port allocation and discovery-heartbeat prerequisites. It is not a new model run of `a1aef7fe3`.

Configuration: Kimi-K3 + natural DSpark3, P8/D8, TP8/DCP8, eager, MoRI RDMA READ, no LMCache; full GSM8K, five-shot, C64, 4096 generated tokens, no limit. P/D each completed 1319 HTTP 200 requests without evaluator retries; external KV use was confirmed. Natural draft acceptance was **96858/126675 (76.4618%)**, with all three positions positive.

Both workload ranks returned 0, phase tokens matched, both cleanup queries returned 0 and container lists were empty. Slurm nevertheless records **FAILED/1:0**, while the workload records **COMPLETED/0**. Results were timestamped 13:46:18 UTC; prefill shutdown began at 13:46:22 and its output-handler `EngineDeadError` occurred at 13:46:34 during teardown. This discrepancy is retained, not counted as clean scheduler shutdown.

Historical evidence from before the allocation rebase and connector-local revision:

| Version | GSM8K Accuracy — Flexible Extract | GSM8K Accuracy — Strict Match |
|---|---:|---:|
| Main without #59164 | 265/1319 — **20.0910%** | 285/1319 — **21.6073%** |
| with #59164 | 1268/1319 — **96.1334%** | 1268/1319 — **96.1334%** |


<details>
<summary>CPU reproduction commands</summary>

From the candidate checkout with a prepared test virtualenv:

```bash
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD"
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_tp_ack.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  -k 'not multi_example_connector_consistency and not fewer_blocks_with_hma and not actual_lmcache and not multi_connector_handle_preemptions_integration and not multi_connector_mixed_hma_disables_hybrid_kv_cache'
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_replay.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  -k 'kv_connector or sync_kv_load or invalid_blocks or prefix_replay or zeroing or external'
```

Model validation ran outside upstream CI on the two-node ROCm runner. The run's matrix artifact records the pinned source and full serving configuration. The boundary test is now collected on CPU without pretending ROCm or MoRI is available.

</details>

## Details

```text
scheduler drains allocation zeroing IDs into a fresh output
  -> connector builds metadata and subtracts full READ destinations
  -> worker zeroes remaining pages and issues READs
  -> existing load barriers wait before the corresponding KV/state is used
```

Hybrid READ metadata already puts the aligned attention group first and excludes local compute tails. The output is built before the metadata hook and dispatched after it; no other connector currently consumes `new_block_ids_to_zero`. MultiConnector passes the same output to its children and gives external tokens only to the selected child. An unselected MoRIIO child has no attention READ destinations to exclude. The exclusion set is local to this call, so later allocations are unaffected.

The interface documentation change is deliberate: the prior unconditional read-only sentence conflicted with this implementation. The exception allows removal of fully overwritten attention blocks only, with load completion before use and step failure on error. Existing hybrid load barriers/failure handling satisfy those obligations. It does not permit changing scheduling counts, block assignments or other fields, or adding pages to the zeroing list.

This change is reversible and its runtime scope remains MoRIIO hybrid READ metadata. READ source ownership and FULL pre-forward context remain separate work.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Share `SchemaRoot` between argument coercion and grammars
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Rust tool parsers coerce raw parameter text by the tool's JSON schema (`tool/parameters.rs`), and argument grammars (#59395) constrain the same parameters by it, but each interpreted the schema on its own. Coercion ignored `$ref`: a parameter whose schema is `{"$ref": "#/$defs/Place"}` came back as the JSON text string `"{\"city\": \"Paris\"}"` instead of an object. Pydantic v2 `model_json_schema()`, which most SDKs use to build tool schemas, emits exactly this for nested models, enums, and `Optional[Model]`:

```json
{"$defs": {"Place": {...}, "Unit": {"enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"], "type": "string"}},
 "properties": {"place": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Place"},
                "unit": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Unit", "default": "celsius"},
                "backup": {"anyOf": [{"$ref": "#/$defs/Place"}, {"type": "null"}], "default": null}}}
```

This affects every schema-coercing parser: Qwen Coder and MiMo, GLM, MiniMax M2/M3, Hy. DeepSeek DSML and Kimi K3 decode by their `string=`/`type=` labels instead. Coercion and grammars also disagreed on `nullable`, `const`, single-schema `allOf`, and type-name aliases such as `"int"`, so a grammar could admit a value that the parser then decodes as another type.

The open-PR search found #50933, which resolves `$ref`/`$defs` for the Python Qwen3-Coder path; there is no Rust counterpart. Python parity is not a goal here. #59190 (the Kimi K3 full-output grammar) is stacked on this PR.

- New `schema::SchemaRoot`, the tool's parameters schema that references resolve against, owns how a parameter's schema is read:
  - `resolved` returns the root after following local `$ref` chains and single-schema `allOf`; unresolvable, cyclic, and remote references accept any value and are never fetched;
  - `options` expands each reference target at most once per value, as the argument grammar walker from #59395 already did, so shared definitions cannot blow up exponentially;
  - `options` splits a value schema into typed options: `const`/`enum` literals, one option per `anyOf`/`oneOf`/type-array alternative, `object`/`array` inferred from `properties`/`items`, `nullable: true` adding `null`, and aliases such as `int` or `dict` parsed to the canonical type;
  - `JsonType` gains `Integer`, since coercion distinguishes integers.
- Argument grammars read value options from `SchemaRoot` instead of their own walker.
- Coercion reads the schema one level at a time. `ToolSchema` keeps the parameters schema, and object and array types resolve their fields and items only when a structured value reaches them. A recursive schema therefore costs only as deep as the value; expanding it ahead of time is exponential in its branching, and a tree with two recursive children took over 60 s to build that way.
- Kimi K3 labels values through its own `xtml_type` mapping, which follows `_xtml_type` in the checkpoint's `encoding_k3.py`; integers and floats are both `number`. Its grammar is unchanged.

Behavior changes in coercion:

- `$ref` resolves at the parameter level, in nested fields and items, and inside `anyOf`.
- `const` and single-schema `allOf` are understood, and `enum` values coerce by their own type, so `"2"` under `{"enum": [1, 2, 3]}` becomes `2`.
- Text that spells a non-string `const` or `enum` value as JSON decodes to that value before any type is tried, so `1` under `{"enum": ["fast", 1]}` becomes the number `1`, as the argument grammar already constrains it, instead of the string `"1"`. Text matching no literal converts as before.
- `anyOf`/`oneOf` whose alternatives all have unknown types now falls back to the raw string, like an unknown `type`, instead of being treated as an object.

Behavior changes in argument grammars (Kimi K3): `nullable: true` admits `type="null"`, an aliased type such as `"int"` constrains its value instead of dropping the parameter, and a schema with `properties` or `items` but no `type` admits only objects or arrays.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
```

- `schema` unit tests: the Pydantic schema above, unresolvable, cyclic, and remote references, aliases in type arrays, `nullable`, mixed enums, single `allOf`, and `items` without `type`.
- Coercion tests: Pydantic-style references (including `Optional` taking `null`), recursive and branching recursive schemas converted from structured values, and integer enums.
- Qwen Coder `parse_complete` with referenced parameters returns an object and an integer.

## Test Result

- `vllm-parser` + `vllm-chat`: 940 tests passed, including all 36 XGrammar replay cases; the roundtrip grammar files are unchanged.
- Workspace Clippy and pre-commit passed.

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build] Widen the ragged prefill scoring tolerance, drop batch invariance
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The ragged-row check in `test_prompt_logprob_token_ids_with_chunking_and_preemption`, added in #56984, compares a second `generate` call against the first at `atol=1e-2`. #60056 stopped it from flaking by forcing `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, which fixed the symptom at the cost of running the test outside the configuration users get. This sets the tolerance from measurement instead and removes the flag. [CI failure log](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/92838/list?sid=01a10aa7-6459-497e-b369-4653327ae8d8&tab=output) 

## Claims

- The flake is gone without pinning kernel selection: 9 runs, 9 passes.
- The tolerance is not arbitrary. The largest deviation I measured is `0.190008`, and `0.2` is the value the unchunked comparison in the same test already uses.
- The check keeps its strength. It exists to catch row misalignment, which is off by nats rather than by hundredths.

## Validation

| Command | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -k token_ids_with_chunking` | passes only with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | `1 passed`, 9 consecutive runs |

Per-run maximum deviation over those runs: `0` in six of them, then `0.173801`, `0.181988` and `0.190008`.

## Details

The deviation is bimodal. Either the second `generate` call lands on the same kernels as the first and the rows come out bit-identical, or it picks different ones and the bf16 tails of these candidates move by a tenth or two. The candidates are arbitrary token ids, so they sit deep in the distribution where that movement is large next to the value itself.

That leaves no room for a stricter bound: `0.2` is about five percent above the largest deviation observed, and anything tighter would flake again.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Backtrack from safe text at a complete marker
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`safe_text_len_mul` (rewritten for token-aware markers in #58358) returns `Incomplete` whenever it has no text to emit. That covers three cases: the input is empty, it starts with a partial marker, or it starts with a complete marker. More input cannot change the last case. So when a caller's marker branches reject that marker, the stream stalls silently until the end and is then flushed as text, instead of failing.

- **Contract:** a complete marker at the start of the input is now `Backtrack`, so `alt` falls through to the other branches, or `parse_buffered_event` reports a parse error. A partial marker or empty input stays `Incomplete`. The rule is documented on `safe_text_len_mul` and pinned by a test.
- **Qwen3 XML:** this was the one caller that hit the new error. Its tool-call branch requires a newline after `<tool_call>`, but its safe text stopped at the bare marker. So `<tool_call>{...` without the newline was held back until the end of the stream. Safe text now stops at the start marker plus its required whitespace (`JsonToolCallWhitespace::Exact`), for both the bare and the framed marker. A lookalike streams as text immediately.
- **`hf`:** its event loop resolves boundaries on either error (stacked on #59005).

All other `safe_text_len*` callers place safe text after their marker branches, so their behavior is unchanged.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --exclude vllm-tool-parser-py -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vllm-tool-parser-py
```

New tests: `utils::tests::safe_text_len_backtracks_at_complete_marker`, and `tool::json::qwen::tests::qwen_xml_streams_start_marker_without_newline_as_text`. The Qwen test checks streaming: the text must be released by `parse_into`, before `finish`. Both fail on the base branch.

## Test Result

- All 1989 workspace tests pass; clippy and fmt are clean. `vllm-tool-parser-py` was excluded because it cannot load `libpython3.14.so` on this host, unrelated to this change.
- Both new tests fail when the change is reverted. The Qwen one fails because the lookalike text is held back (`left: ""`).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Let pooling chunked prefill use full context
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

- Fix a V1 scheduler liveness bug for pooling requests with chunked prefill.
- Pooling runners emit an output from the final prefill hidden state and do not append a sampled token, but the scheduler reserved one context slot for every non-diffusion request.
- When a pooling prompt length equaled `max_model_len`, the first chunk could run, the next running-step schedule would stop one token early, and the request could no longer make progress.
- Reserve zero sampled-token slots for pooling runners so the final prefill chunk can reach `max_model_len` and emit the pooling output.

Fixes #47971, Fixes #24704, Fixes #55427

- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search 'repo:vllm-project/vllm 24704 in:body'` returned no open PRs.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Return 4xx for client errors in /cohere/v2/chat
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`POST /cohere/v2/chat` and `POST /cohere/v2/chat/render` answer every exception raised while handling a request with HTTP 500, including errors caused by the request itself. `/v1/chat/completions` returns 400 for the same input. This routes the exception through `create_error_response`, the way #52246 did for `/v1/messages`.

Fixes #60304

## Claims

- Client-caused errors raised by the Cohere chat and render handlers (`VLLMValidationError`, `pydantic.ValidationError`, and the other cases `create_error_response` maps to 4xx) now return 4xx instead of 500, e.g. `temperature: -1` or a `seed` outside int64.
- The response body keeps the Cohere `{message, id}` envelope.
- Unexpected errors still return 500 with the same body as before.
- The Cohere SDK retries every status >= 500 (`_should_retry` in `cohere/core/http_client.py`, cohere 7.2.0), so a malformed request is no longer replayed by SDK clients.

## Validation

Reproduced on current `main` (bf049ddb8f) with FastAPI's `TestClient` and vLLM's global exception handlers installed. `/v1/chat/completions` gets the same input for comparison.

| input | route | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seed = 2**63` | `/cohere/v2/chat` | 500 | 400 |
| `seed = 2**63` | `/cohere/v2/chat/render` | 500 | 400 |
| `seed = 2**63` | `/v1/chat/completions` | 400 | 400 |
| `temperature = -1` | `/cohere/v2/chat` | 500 | 400 |
| `temperature = -1` | `/v1/chat/completions` | 400 | 400 |
| `temperature = 5` | `/cohere/v2/chat` | 500 | 400 |
| `temperature = 5` | `/v1/chat/completions` | 400 | 400 |

- `seed = 2**63` fails `ChatCompletionRequest` validation while the v2 body is converted, using the real `CohereServingChatV2` conversion with no engine.
- The `temperature` rows go through the real `create_chat_v2` -> `create_chat_completion` -> `to_sampling_params` path, with the renderer and engine client stubbed out. Both routes return the same message, e.g. `temperature must be non-negative, got -1.0. (parameter=temperature, value=-1.0)`. The Cohere body is `{"message": ..., "id": "chatcmpl-..."}`.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script for the seed case</summary>

```python
import os

os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API"] = "1"

from argparse import Namespace

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from vllm.entrypoints.cohere.api_router import attach_router

from vllm.entrypoints.serve.exception_handling.register import init_exception_handler

app.state.args = Namespace(
    log_error_stack=False, enable_scale_out=True, tokens_only=False
)
init_exception_handler(app)
attach_router(app)
app.state.cohere_serving_chat_v2 = CohereServingChatV2.__new__(CohereServingChatV2)

body = {"model": "m", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], "seed": 2**63}
with TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False) as client:
    r = client.post("/cohere/v2/chat", json=body)
    print(r.status_code, r.text)
```

</details>

Regression tests, added to `tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_api_router.py`:

- `TestEndpoint::test_handler_client_error_returns_400_envelope` (parametrized: `VLLMValidationError`, `ValueError`)
- `TestRenderEndpoint::test_conversion_client_error_returns_400_envelope` (the existing `test_conversion_exception_returns_500_envelope`, which asserted 500 for a conversion `ValueError`, now asserts 400)

With only the tests applied on top of `main`'s `api_router.py`, all three fail because the route returns 500 where the test expects 400:

```text

FAILED ...::TestEndpoint::test_handler_client_error_returns_400_envelope[vllm_validation_error]

```

With the fix they pass, and so do the existing `RuntimeError` -> 500 tests (`test_handler_exception_returns_500_envelope`, `test_render_exception_returns_500_envelope`).

`pytest tests/entrypoints/cohere --ignore=tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_chat_v2.py`: 217 passed with the change. `test_chat_v2.py` boots a server with model weights and was not run.

Re-checked after rebasing onto `e37e51dd24` (current `main`):

- The three `client_error` tests fail with `api_router.py` reverted to `main` (`assert 500 == <HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST: 400>`) and pass with the fix.
- The `seed` and `temperature` repros still return 500 on `/cohere/v2/chat` and 400 on `/v1/chat/completions` on `main`.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/cohere --ignore=tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_chat_v2.py`: 217 passed.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_api_router.py vllm/entrypoints/cohere/api_router.py`, which runs every hook CI runs (including `mypy` for Python 3.10 to 3.13): all hooks pass.

## Details

Root cause: both handlers in `vllm/entrypoints/cohere/api_router.py` (the `except Exception` blocks at lines 141 and 197 on `main`) built a fixed `HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` response, with the comment "report as 500 for parity". `/v1/messages` had the same hard-coded 500 until #52246 switched it to `create_error_response`. The OpenAI routes never catch the exception and let the global handlers map it, so the same bad input produced 400 there and 500 here. The conversion in `create_chat_v2` and `to_sampling_params` in the chat path both run outside any handler that would turn their exceptions into an `ErrorResponse`, so they reach this `except`.

The fix replaces the hard-coded response with `_error_response(create_error_response(e), raw_request)`. `create_error_response` is the mapper the global exception handlers and `/v1/messages` use: client-error `VLLMError` subclasses and the legacy `ValueError`/`TypeError`/`OverflowError` fallbacks map to 4xx, `NotImplementedError` to 501, server-side `VLLMError`s keep their 5xx status, and anything else is 500 with the same message as before. `_error_response` already builds the `CohereError` body, so the wire shape is unchanged. The stale `noqa` comment is dropped along with the wrong "parity" claim.

Scope and limits:

- Only the two `except` blocks change. The `ErrorResponse` branch and `CohereErrorEnvelopeMiddleware` are untouched.
- Like the shared handlers, a stray `ValueError` raised by an internal bug is now reported as 400 rather than 500.
- The existing `logger.exception` calls are kept, so client errors are still logged with a traceback, as in `/v1/messages`.

Not a duplicate: I searched `vllm-project/vllm` issues and PRs, open and closed, for combinations of `cohere`, `/cohere/v2/chat`, `api_router`, 500, 4xx, client error, `create_error_response`, `seed` and `temperature`, and listed all `cohere in:title,body` PRs. No issue or PR covers the Cohere status mapping. Closest hits:

- #52246 (merged): the same fix for `/v1/messages`; this follows its approach.
- #52622 (merged): the same for `/detokenize`.
- #57018 (open): bounds `seed` in `CohereChatV2Request` and `SamplingParams`. It closes one trigger at the schema level; this change covers the other errors reaching the same `except` (e.g. `temperature`), and the two do not overlap in code.
- #55489 (open): changes one line inside the render route's `try` block (passes `raw_request` to `render_chat_request`); no change to the error handling.
- #52467, #53750, #56146 (merged) and #52437 (open): validate fields of the Cohere request model, before the handler runs.

This PR was co-authored with Claude.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DCP] Default MLA DCP verify to the round-robin asm decode where it applies
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

#56861 added the AITER round-robin asm decode (`cprr`) for causal multi-token verify under decode context
parallelism, but left `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` defaulting to `segmented`, which expands every verify token
into its own paged-KV row. At realistic batch sizes `segmented` is much slower, so DCP + speculative decoding is not
worth enabling on MI355X with the default.

This PR adds `auto` as the new default: use `cprr` wherever `_asm_dcp_verify_configured` holds (gfx950, DCP with
interleave 1, speculative decoding) and the gathered head count is servable, otherwise `segmented`. Explicit `asm`
and `segmented` behave as before (`asm` still raises on an unservable shape; `auto` raises only if neither route can
serve the batch). The unservable-shape error now names the configured route and only suggests `segmented` when the
AITER build supports it. It also lower-cases the value before comparing: `env_with_choices(case_sensitive=False)` validates
case-insensitively but returns the raw string, so `ASM` silently meant `segmented`.

## Test Result

Kimi-K3 (MXFP4), 8x MI355X, TP8 / DCP8 (a2a), DSpark k=4.

Verify route microbenchmark (60k shared prefix + 4k unique, OSL 256, 48 prompts, conc 48, same node and image):

| verify route | output tok/s | median TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|
| `segmented` (current default) | 141.0 | 170.8 ms |
| `cprr` (this PR's default) | 212.6 | 101.0 ms |

At OSL 1024 `segmented` completed no request inside the benchmark window.

InferenceX agentic-coding trace, conc 48 (synthetic acceptance length 3.36, as in InferenceX CI):

| configuration | tot tok/s/GPU | interactivity p90 | TPOT p50 | e2e p50 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DCP8, no spec, 900 s | 12,317 | 19.1 | 38 ms | 13.1 s |
| DCP8 + DSpark k=4 on `cprr`, 900 s | 13,551 (+10.0%) | 21.6 | 20 ms | 7.0 s |
| DCP8 + DSpark k=4 on `cprr`, 3600 s, CI warmup | 14,903 | 19.3 | 28 ms | 9.0 s |
| InferenceX CI MI355X c48 (no spec), for reference | 12,090 | 14.7 | 49 ms | 18.1 s |

The 900 s rows are on the same node; the 3600 s row also includes other open K3 PRs in the test image
(#58861, #59070) and `--stream-interval 10`.

### Accuracy

gsm8k 5-shot, 1319 questions, `lm_eval --model local-completions` against the served model, `num_concurrent=64`;
Kimi-K3 MXFP4, 8x MI355X, TP8 / DCP8 (a2a), FP8 KV cache, async scheduling, FULL CUDA graphs. The test base is vLLM 36768d1b plus the open K3 PRs
#58861 and #59070 and merged #56960 #59175 #58344. Spec runs use DSpark k=4 with real (block) rejection, so acceptance length reflects actual draft quality.

| configuration | strict-match | flexible-extract | mean acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| no speculative decoding (test base without #58887) | 0.9568 ± 0.0056 | — | — |
| DSpark k=4, `cprr` forced via env, without this PR (vLLM 36768d1b + #58887) | 0.9568 ± 0.0056 | 0.9568 | 3.78 |

The no-spec run predates #58887 and scored normally; the spec runs need it. Bases older than #58887 (merged 2026-10-01) lose accuracy with DCP + spec at this concurrency
regardless of this PR (gsm8k 0.90-0.93; see #58886).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Index Mamba align state copies by request slot in MRV2
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix Mamba "align" state copies reading another request's block ids under MRV2 + PP + MTP, which poisons recurrent state (all-NaN logits, constant-token output, acceptance collapse). Consolidates #55506 and #57807 into a smaller change; both authors are co-authors. Refs #54173.

## Claims

- The precopy/postprocess state-copy kernels index the persistent per-request-slot block tables by `req_idx`, so a postprocess that runs steps after its batch (non-last PP rank) no longer reads tables re-gathered for a later batch.
- `compute_aligned_state_indices` is unchanged: it still reads the gathered batch-order tables, so padded rows and CUDA graph capture behave as on main.
- The align context is built once in `initialize_kv_cache` instead of lazily from whichever caller runs first, which removes the capture-time / profiling binding issues raised on #55506 and #57807.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_precopy_mamba_align.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py`: 146 passed (GB200).
- With the kernels reverted to batch-row indexing, the new/updated kernel tests fail (26 failures), so they cover the bug.
- E2E on GB200, Qwen3.6-27B, MRV2, MTP 4, `--async-scheduling --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align` (reproduction from @tomasruizt on #55506). main = upstream 31e2443.

| | GSM8K 5-shot (mqa, chat, no think) | Mean acceptance length (completions GSM8K / bench) | Output tok/s (random 2k/1k, c=8) | Mean TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main, PP=2 | did not finish: 8 requests stuck at AL 1.00 (no draft accepted) for 15 min at 772/1319, cancelled | 2.95 / 3.56 | 1177 | 5.50 ms |
| this PR, PP=2 | 0.9727 strict / 0.9719 flexible | 4.13 / 4.42 | 1506 | 4.76 ms |
| this PR, PP=1 (reference) | 0.9727 strict / 0.9719 flexible | 4.13 / 4.35 | 1589 | 4.46 ms |

  The stuck requests on main are the constant-token loop from poisoned recurrent state; with a 4096 max-token cap, main PP=2 averaged 235 output tokens per GSM8K question vs 82 for this PR at PP=2 and PP=1. The fix does not change kernel work; the throughput gain comes from the recovered acceptance length.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B --language-model-only \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --async-scheduling --enable-prefix-caching \
  --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 4}'
# PP=1 reference: drop --pipeline-parallel-size 2

vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0.75 \
  --random-prefix-len 1024 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 42 \
  --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 8

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319 \
  --max-concurrency 64   # acceptance length column; accuracy from mqa gsm8k (5-shot, chat, no thinking)
```

Acceptance length is `1 + spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens / spec_decode_num_drafts` from `/metrics`.
</details>

## Details

Root cause: `MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext` captures block-table pointers once. MRV2 bound it to `input_block_tables`, a single buffer re-gathered in batch order every step, and the copy kernels indexed it by batch row. On a non-last PP rank the postprocess for step N runs after step N+k has re-gathered that buffer, so batch rows point at other requests' blocks. With the unified hybrid cache layout those copies land in live state.

Why not just #55506 or #57807: both keep lazy binding and add machinery around it (temporary bindings / `bind` flag, or two lazily bound contexts plus profiling teardown), and #55506 remaps the aligned-index kernel through `idx_mapping`, which changes padded-row behavior. Binding both table sets eagerly avoids all of that. The source tables are safe to read late because a request is not rescheduled (so its row is not rewritten or its slot reused) until its in-flight step's output is processed.

MRV1 is unaffected: it launches both kernels without `idx_mapping`, where `req_idx == batch_idx`, and passes a single table set, which stays the default for the aligned-index tables.

Credit: root cause first identified by @zebgop-ops; fix direction and kernel tests from @Karl0007 (#55506); separate metadata/copy tables and the profiling lifetime issue from @yongqinwang-cmd (#57807).

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MRV2] Avoid stream syncs in NonUvaBuffer host-to-device copies
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #58849. `NonUvaBuffer`, the MRV2 buffer fallback when pinned memory is unavailable (WSL2 by default), copies its host buffer to the GPU with a blocking `copy_()`. This makes the copy `non_blocking`, as V1's `CpuGpuBuffer.copy_to_gpu` already does for pageable memory. The root cause and the two-line fix come from @joynerwk03 in the issue (co-author on the commit).

## Claims

- Removes the `cudaStreamSynchronize` after every `NonUvaBuffer.uva()` copy (~16 per decode step), so preparing step N+1 no longer waits for step N to finish.
- WSL2 with the default V2 runner: decode step time **-13.7% at batch 1 and -12.5% at batch 16** on an RTX 4050, the same as `VLLM_WSL2_ENABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1`. The reporter measured -12% on an RTX 3090.
- No change where pinned memory is available: those platforms use `UvaBuffer`.

## Validation

**Regression test** `tests/kernels/core/test_uva.py::test_non_uva_buffer_copies_without_stream_sync`: copies under `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")`, overwrites the host buffer right away, then checks the GPU values. On main it fails with `RuntimeError: called a synchronizing CUDA operation`; with this PR it passes.

**End to end**, main `888074b4` vs this PR: Qwen3-0.6B, default V2 runner, default compile and CUDA graphs, RTX 4050 Laptop 6 GB, WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04, driver 581.86), torch 2.13.0+cu130. Arms alternated, 3 fresh engines per arm; each engine ran 2 warmup and 8 timed `LLM.generate` calls of 256 greedy tokens (`ignore_eos`).

| Decode step, median of 3 engines (range) | main | this PR | main + `VLLM_WSL2_ENABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Batch 1 | 8.83 ms (8.68-8.91) | **7.61 ms** (7.43-7.67) | 7.64 ms (7.63-7.65) |
| Batch 16 | 10.98 ms (10.67-11.02) | **9.61 ms** (9.44-9.71) | 9.67 ms (9.66-9.84) |

**Outputs.** Comparing greedy outputs across restarts is confounded by #58899 (Inductor re-tunes reductions by timing), so I kept one engine alive (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`) and swapped `NonUvaBuffer.uva` between the blocking and `non_blocking` versions for four rounds of 16 prompts x 128 tokens: token ids and top-5 logprobs were bitwise identical in every round, in two separate engines (main `840c7c2`; `buffer_utils.py` is unchanged since).

## Details

Why the async copy is safe:
- **Stream ordering.** Every reader of a `NonUvaBuffer` GPU slot runs on the copy's stream, or on a side stream that calls `wait_stream` on it first (async output, spec decode and PP copy streams). This is from reading the code; ubatch/DBO, PP and DeepSeek-V4.1 paths were not exercised.
- **Reusing the host buffer.** The next step overwrites `cpu` right after the copy is issued. For pageable memory the driver stages the copy into pinned memory during the call, synchronizing with the stream when it has to ([CUDA API sync behavior](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/api-sync-behavior.html)); V1's `CpuGpuBuffer` relies on the same behavior. Measured on this driver: with a `non_blocking` pageable copy issued behind a ~7.5 ms GPU sleep and the source overwritten immediately, 0/200 results were corrupted from 4 B to 16 MiB (pinned control: 200/200). Copies up to 64 KiB were staged at call time and returned immediately; larger ones waited for the stream, keeping today's cost. `NonUvaBuffer` copies are far below 64 KiB.
- **`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK`.** Its copy checker flags every `non_blocking` copy from unpinned memory as possibly synchronous, so it flags `NonUvaBuffer` both before and after this change. I left the copy outside `gpu_sync_allowed()` so the checker keeps reporting it.

Not tested: native Linux without pinned memory, other drivers, TP/PP.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3] Fence decode indexer shared-memory stage reuse
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add the missing generic-to-async proxy fences before the decode indexer
releases its Q and K shared-memory stages for TMA reuse.

## Claims

- Prevents wrong indexer scores under concurrent GPU writes.
- Extends the existing indexer correctness test; no new test harness or file.

## Validation

B200, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13, CUTLASS DSL 4.7.1:

- The six decode-indexer pytest cases pass.
- In five fresh processes, the concurrent-write test failed without the fences
  and passed with them. Each fixed run checks 20 stressed launches.
- Quiet baseline and fixed outputs are bitwise identical for the stress input.
- Three alternating timing runs, 1,000 launches each: baseline means
  14.698 / 14.567 / 14.550 us; fixed 14.593 / 14.551 / 14.516 us.
  No measurable slowdown at this shape. These are kernel timings, not an
  end-to-end serving measurement.

Test selector in a matching vLLM development environment:

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py \
        -k decode_index_score_cutedsl_correctness -v

## Details

The consumer reads through ldmatrix (generic proxy), while the producer
refills through TMA (async proxy). Releasing the empty-stage barrier does not
by itself establish the needed cross-proxy ordering. Fence before both
releases, including the Q tile that aliases K stage zero.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Log the full request body when max_log_len is unset
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `--enable-log-requests` at DEBUG level, the request JSON body log added in #58163 drops the last character of every body when `--max-log-len` is unset, which is the default. The closing `}` is missing, so the logged line is not valid JSON. This slices the body with `max_log_len` as is, so `None` keeps the whole body.

Fixes #60305

## Claims

- With the default `--max-log-len`, the DEBUG `Request <id> JSON body: ...` line contains the complete body and parses as JSON.
- With `--max-log-len N`, the body is still cut to its first `N` characters.

## Validation

There was no GPU available, so this was not checked against a live `vllm serve`. Instead I called `BaseServing._check_model`, which is where the serving paths call `log_request_body`, with `RequestLogger(max_log_len=None)`, the logger at DEBUG and a `ChatCompletionRequest` with one user message:

```
# main (bf049ddb8f)
Request ae92dec5c10116ec JSON body: {"messages":[{"content":"Say hello.","role":"user"}],"model":"test-model"
logged body is NOT valid JSON: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 74 (char 73)

# this PR
Request b632ee1a8e84b1f6 JSON body: {"messages":[{"content":"Say hello.","role":"user"}],"model":"test-model"}
logged body is valid JSON
```

Calling `RequestLogger.log_request_body` directly on `CompletionRequest(model="test-model", prompt="Hello, world!")`:

```
# main
max_log_len=None  : ... JSON body: {"model":"test-model","prompt":"Hello, world!","max_tokens":16
max_log_len=10    : ... JSON body: {"model":"

# this PR
max_log_len=None  : ... JSON body: {"model":"test-model","prompt":"Hello, world!","max_tokens":16}
max_log_len=10    : ... JSON body: {"model":"
```

`max_log_len=0` (empty body) and `max_log_len=10000` (full body) give the same output on both.

The example logs in #58163's description show the same missing closing brace (e.g. `..."stream":false,"temperature":0.0`).

Regression test `test_request_logger_log_request_body_truncation` in `tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_request_logger.py`, parametrized over `max_log_len` in `[None, 10]`. With the new test and the old `request_logger.py`:

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_request_logger.py
.........F.
FAILED ...::test_request_logger_log_request_body_truncation[None]
E         - _tokens":16}
E         ?            -
E         + _tokens":16
1 failed, 10 passed
```

With this PR, `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/utils` gives `41 passed` (the 39 existing tests and the two new cases).

Re-checked after rebasing onto `e37e51dd24` (current `main`):

- `test_request_logger_log_request_body_truncation[None]` fails with `request_logger.py` reverted to `main` (the logged body ends in `_tokens":16` instead of `_tokens":16}`) and passes with the fix.
- The repro above still logs the body without its closing brace on `main`.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/utils`: 41 passed.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_request_logger.py vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/request_logger.py`, which runs every hook CI runs (including `mypy` for Python 3.10 to 3.13): all hooks pass.

## Details

Root cause: `log_request_body` (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/request_logger.py`) turned an unset `max_log_len` into `-1` and used it as the slice end, so `[:-1]` removed the last character instead of meaning "no limit". `--max-log-len` documents `None` as unlimited, and `log_inputs` and `log_outputs` in the same class leave their text alone when it is `None`. Slicing with `None` already keeps the whole string, so the `-1` mapping is simply dropped. Nothing else changes: the DEBUG gate and log format are the same, and `max_log_len=0` still logs an empty body.

Not a duplicate. I searched issues and PRs in `vllm-project/vllm` for `log_request_body`, `request_logger.py`, `max_log_len`, `request JSON body` and `enable-log-requests`, and found nothing that reports or fixes this. Closest:

- #58163 (merged) introduced the body log.
- #45634 (open) adds request arrival and completion logs to `RequestLogger`; it does not touch `log_request_body`.
- #58573 (closed, unmerged) correlates request logs with external request IDs; it does not touch `log_request_body`.

This PR was co-authored with Claude.

from vllm.v1.engine.async_llm import AsyncLLM

        speculative_config={"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
                            "prompt_lookup_min": 1, "prompt_lookup_max": 3},
        per_request_spec_decode_metrics="summary",
    ))
    prompt = ("<|im_start|>user\n/no_think\n"
              "Repeat the phrase red blue green fifty times, separated by spaces. "
              "Output only the repeated words.\n<|im_end|>\n"
              "<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\n")
    params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=128, ignore_eos=True,
                            output_kind=RequestOutputKind.DELTA)

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor default penalties in batch chat completions
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/v1/chat/completions/batch` ignores server-default `presence_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` (from `generation_config.json` or `--override-generation-config`) because `BatchChatCompletionRequest` still defaults both fields to `0.0`. This applies to the batch request the same `None` defaults that #50769 gave `ChatCompletionRequest` and `CompletionRequest`, in the same way #47597 did for `temperature`, `top_p`, `min_p` and `repetition_penalty`.

Fixes #60302

## Claims

- An omitted `presence_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` on `/v1/chat/completions/batch` now resolves to the server default, exactly as on `/v1/chat/completions`.
- Explicit client values still win, including an explicit `0.0`.
- With no server default the penalties stay `0.0`, so behavior without a generation config does not change.
- Two-line change in `protocol.py`, plus a regression test.

## Validation

Repro on `main` (`bf049ddb8f`), server defaults `presence_penalty=0.5`, `frequency_penalty=0.25`, client omits both:

```python
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import (
    BatchChatCompletionRequest, ChatCompletionRequest)

conv = [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]
server_defaults = {"presence_penalty": 0.5, "frequency_penalty": 0.25}

sp = ChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=conv).to_sampling_params(16, server_defaults)
print("single  :", sp.presence_penalty, sp.frequency_penalty)

batch = BatchChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=[conv])
print("batch field defaults:", batch.presence_penalty, batch.frequency_penalty)
sp = batch.to_chat_completion_request(conv).to_sampling_params(16, server_defaults)
print("batch   :", sp.presence_penalty, sp.frequency_penalty)
```

```text
# main                                  # this PR
single  : 0.5 0.25                      single  : 0.5 0.25
batch field defaults: 0.0 0.0           batch field defaults: None None
batch   : 0.0 0.0                       batch   : 0.5 0.25
```

With no server default (`to_sampling_params(16, {})`) the converted batch request gets `0.0 0.0` on both `main` and this PR, and an explicit `presence_penalty=0.0, frequency_penalty=0.0` on the batch request gives `0.0 0.0` even with the server defaults above.

The same through `OpenAIServingChatBatch.create_batch_chat_completion` with a mocked engine whose model config reports `{"presence_penalty": 0.5, "frequency_penalty": 0.25}`, printing the `SamplingParams` handed to `engine.generate`:

```text
# main                                          # this PR
/v1/chat/completions       : 0.5 0.25           /v1/chat/completions       : 0.5 0.25
/v1/chat/completions/batch : 0.0 0.0            /v1/chat/completions/batch : 0.5 0.25
batch, explicit 1.0 / 0.0  : 1.0 0.0            batch, explicit 1.0 / 0.0  : 1.0 0.0
```

Regression test: `TestBatchChatCompletionPenaltyDefaults` in `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_penalty_default_resolution.py` (existing file, already collected by the `entrypoints/openai` Buildkite step).

- On `main`, `test_defaults_applied_when_client_omits` fails with `assert 0.0 == 1.5` (`presence_penalty`) and the other six tests in the file pass.
- With the fix, all seven tests in the file pass.

Test runs on CPU, with the fix applied (the last selector is the five mock-engine tests in `test_batched_chat_completions.py`, the ones marked `skip_global_cleanup`):

```text
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/test_penalty_default_resolution.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/test_watermarking.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat.py::test_null_top_logprobs_is_same_as_omitted \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py::<five mock-engine tests>
-> 77 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_error.py
-> 31 passed
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k "not gpt_oss"
-> 180 passed, 11 deselected
```

No failures. Not run: the 11 `gpt_oss` tests in `test_serving_chat.py` (they start a real `gpt-oss-20b` server) and the server-backed tests in `test_batched_chat_completions.py`, which need a GPU.

Re-checked after rebasing onto `e37e51dd24` (current `main`):

- `TestBatchChatCompletionPenaltyDefaults::test_defaults_applied_when_client_omits` fails with `protocol.py` reverted to `main` (`assert 0.0 == 1.5`) and passes with the fix.
- The request-level repro above still prints `0.0 0.0` for the batch request on `main`.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/test_penalty_default_resolution.py` plus the five mock-engine tests in `test_batched_chat_completions.py`: 12 passed.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files tests/entrypoints/openai/test_penalty_default_resolution.py vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py`, which runs every hook CI runs (including `mypy` for Python 3.10 to 3.13): all hooks pass.

## Details

`BatchChatCompletionRequest.to_chat_completion_request()` builds each per-conversation request from `self.model_dump(exclude={"messages"}, exclude_none=True)`, so every non-`None` field default is forwarded as if the client had set it. `presence_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` defaulted to `0.0` (`protocol.py`, `BatchChatCompletionRequest`), so `ChatCompletionRequest.to_sampling_params()` always saw `0.0` and never consulted `default_sampling_params`. #50769 added both names to `ModelConfig.get_diff_sampling_param()` and made the fields `None` on `ChatCompletionRequest` and `CompletionRequest`, but the batch request kept the old default. The batch request's own comment says it mirrors `ChatCompletionRequest`; this restores that.

The fix sets both fields to `None`. `exclude_none=True` then drops them from the converted request, and the existing resolution order applies: client value, then server default, then the OpenAI default of `0.0`. Nothing else reads these two fields from the batch request.

Scope: only the two field defaults. The request schema default for these two fields changes from `0.0` to `None` (a client that omits them still gets `0.0` unless the operator configured a default).

Not a duplicate. Searched `vllm-project/vllm` issues and PRs (open, merged and closed) for: `batch penalty`, `chat completions batch`, `BatchChatCompletionRequest`, `presence_penalty batch`, `frequency_penalty batch chat`, `presence_penalty override-generation-config`, `frequency_penalty generation_config`, `penalty defaults chat batch endpoint`, `to_chat_completion_request penalty`, `batch endpoint default sampling params`, plus `gh pr list --state open --search` for `BatchChatCompletionRequest`, `chat_completion/protocol.py presence_penalty` and `presence_penalty`. Closest hits:

- #47597 (merged): same bug class on the batch request for `temperature`, `top_p`, `min_p`, `repetition_penalty`; it did not touch the penalties, which were still `0.0` on `ChatCompletionRequest` at the time.
- #50769 (merged, fixes issue #50767): fixed the single-conversation and completions paths. A comment on that PR expected the batch defaults to be inert because `check_batch_mode` dumps with `exclude_unset=True`. They are not: that dump only feeds validation, the model still gets the `0.0` field default, and `to_chat_completion_request()` dumps with `exclude_none=True`, which keeps it (see the repro above).
- #50042 (open PR): adds `stream` / `tools` validation to `BatchChatCompletionRequest`; different fields, no overlap.
- #54469 (open PR): server-default `thinking_token_budget`; different fields.
- #57935, #50026 (open issues): other batch endpoint bugs, unrelated to sampling defaults.

This PR was co-authored with Claude.
