commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] Skip padded work in block-FP8 DeepGEMM experts
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Skip padded work in block-FP8 `DeepGemmExperts` on SM90 and SM100-family GPUs. Both grouped GEMMs use DeepGEMM's prefix-sum scheduler, and fused SiLU/SwiGLU activation quantization consumes the same live expert endpoints. This avoids visiting unused padded GEMM tiles and quantizing the full allocated workspace when only a fraction contains live rows.

The shared permutation helper produces expert endpoints for both architectures. SM100 dispatch uses packed UE8M0 activation scales; SM90 dispatch uses the column-major FP32 activation-scale path, including plain and power-of-two-rounded scales. The dispatch remains limited to block-FP8 weights and supported fused gated activations. `mk_alignment_scope` and DeepGEMM's default `ensure_zero_padding=True` remain in place. Other paths keep their existing behavior.

## Relationship to existing work

This PR now includes the SM90 work from #59220 alongside the SM100 work. The latest commit restores the exact combined source tree tested before those paths were split; #59220 is being closed as superseded. #59044 enables prefix sums for FP4 weights on SM10.x but leaves FP8 callers unchanged. The shared permutation and packed-activation helpers from that PR are included here for review against main and should be reconciled when it lands. #54109 changes the padded activation-format contract and targets the FP4 DeepGEMM caller; it does not wire both FP8 GEMMs and fused activation to these endpoints. No issue is closed.

## Validation

The GPU runs used the combined implementation before the split. The final commit restores that same source tree; local pre-commit, mypy, and `git diff --check` passed after restoration. Validation overlaid three changed source files onto a pinned vLLM image rather than rebuilding current main. DeepGEMM binaries and headers were unchanged.

### SM100 on B200

Two independent single-B200 runs used Pirate (`b200-02`) and Pirate2 (`dell-b200-02`). The full-expert graph regression compared the existing FP8 scheduler with prefix sums during CUDA-graph replay, including changing routing, one live row, empty routing, GPU token-count metadata, and poisoned workspaces. Packed activation tests checked live values and scales, untouched gaps, clamping, empty experts, and changing endpoints. **75 tests passed on each cluster** (32.18 s and 39.48 s), before the SM90 extension. A later B200 run of the combined source passed 123 tests covering the packed and column-major paths, before two direct GEMM tests were added.

The full-expert benchmark covered permutation, both GEMMs, activation quantization, and unpermutation/reduction, using 32 experts, FP8 E4M3 weights with 128×128 scales, intermediate size 2,048, hidden size 7,168, top-k 8, and BF16 inputs/outputs. CUPTI kernel-span timings of captured CUDA graphs used cold L2 and 100 measured samples per arm across four alternating rounds; allocation, compilation, and capture were excluded. In the heavily padded 512-capacity / 16-live-token case, latency improved from 472.176 to 347.456 µs on Pirate and 469.101 to 344.942 µs on Pirate2 (26.4–26.5%). At 4,096 / 4,096 tokens, it improved from 1,570.834 to 1,509.025 µs and 1,590.503 to 1,513.257 µs (3.9–4.9%). All benchmark outputs matched bit for bit.

Paired full GSM8K evaluation used `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-block` at revision `6b2399be90eff484848cbbabd684930e01400d54`: all 1,319 questions, five-shot, greedy, seed 42, at most 256 output tokens and 64 sequences, model length 8,192, TP1/EP1, BF16 KV cache, `moe_backend=deep_gemm`, and full/piecewise CUDA graphs. Pirate baseline/optimized accuracy was 1,176/1,319 (89.158%) and 1,182/1,319 (89.613%); Pirate2 was 1,178/1,319 (89.310%) and 1,176/1,319 (89.158%). All runs passed the 85% threshold. Generated token sequences matched on 810 and 805 questions, respectively. These results do not establish bitwise model equivalence or an accuracy improvement.

### SM90 on H200

The SM90 regression covers both projections leaving unused output capacity untouched, changing routing and endpoints during CUDA-graph replay, empty routing, and both plain and rounded FP32 column-major activation scales. **125 tests passed for each scale mode** on one Waldorf H200. These runs used the combined implementation. The pinned DeepGEMM prefix-sum scheduler skips unused whole tiles; padding within a partially filled tile remains. All measured full-expert outputs matched bit for bit.

Using the same full-expert benchmark shape and timing method, the 512-capacity / 16-live-token case improved from 694.415 to 438.144 µs with plain FP32 scales and 694.735 to 438.735 µs with rounded FP32 scales (about 37%). At 4,096 / 4,096 tokens, it improved from 2,874.813 to 2,646.141 µs and 2,935.535 to 2,739.246 µs (6.7–8.0%). A ten-shape activation-only comparison found no material regression in the ordinary dense path. Expert metadata added roughly 0.3–1.8 µs for some fully occupied small shapes.

Paired full GSM8K used the same pinned model and revision, 1,319 questions, five-shot greedy decoding, seed 42, at most 256 output tokens and 256 sequences, model length 8,192, TP1/EP1, BF16 KV cache, `moe_backend=deep_gemm`, full/piecewise CUDA graphs, and rounded FP32 activation scales. Baseline accuracy was 1,180/1,319 (89.462%); optimized accuracy was 1,181/1,319 (89.538%). Both exceeded 85%, and 1,317 generated token sequences matched exactly. This was an accuracy check, not a model-throughput benchmark or evidence of improved accuracy.

### Commands and scope

GPU commands were run with the pinned container's `/tmp/check/.venv/bin/python`, with extracted tests in `/tmp/bundle` and source overlays under `/tmp/overlay`:

```bash
# B200: tests, benchmark, and paired model evaluation for each variant
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/overlay /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/bundle/test_fp8.py /tmp/bundle/test_activation.py -q --disable-warnings --junitxml=/tmp/bundle/pytest.xml
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/overlay /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python /tmp/bundle/benchmark.py
FP8_VARIANT=dense PYTHONPATH=/tmp/eval_dense /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python /tmp/bundle/model_eval.py
FP8_VARIANT=prefix PYTHONPATH=/tmp/eval_prefix /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python /tmp/bundle/model_eval.py

# H200: repeat tests and benchmark once for each scale mode
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0 PYTHONPATH=/tmp/overlay /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/bundle/test_fp8.py /tmp/bundle/test_activation.py -q
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1 PYTHONPATH=/tmp/overlay /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/bundle/test_fp8.py /tmp/bundle/test_activation.py -q
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0 PYTHONPATH=/tmp/overlay /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python /tmp/bundle/benchmark.py
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1 PYTHONPATH=/tmp/overlay /tmp/check/.venv/bin/python /tmp/bundle/benchmark.py
```

`test_fp8.py` extracts the relevant tests and helpers from `tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py` and `tests/kernels/moe/utils.py` to avoid unrelated test-package dependencies; `test_activation.py` copies the activation suite. Local checks on the restored combined tree:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_per_token_group_quant_fp8_colmajor.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/deep_gemm_moe.py vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/deep_gemm_moe.py vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py
git diff --check
```

The pinned runtime was `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:f29125bcc6d276ed38a67c9dfd4e51ccbaba09ad92847a0913c0df38d9c05c71`, vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9`; source changes were based on `953f90d25f`. B200 and H200 were tested. SM103, SM120 fallback execution, and distributed DeepEP V2 were not tested. Synthetic expert latency is not end-to-end serving throughput. Both clusters' model and benchmark artifacts are preserved under local `repros/block-fp8-padding-20260928/` and `repros/block-fp8-sm90-20260929/`; H200 artifacts are also on Waldorf PVC `synthid-bench-results` under `/block-fp8-sm90-padding-20260929/`.

commits.pr_title: [Attention] Add UltraQuant 4-bit KV cache backend (FlyDSL D=256)
commits.pr_body: ## Purpose Adds an `ultraquant_4bit` KV-cache dtype for long-context / agentic serving, where the KV cache is the limiter. UltraQuant stores the cache at 4 bits, FP4 E2M1 codes with UE8M0 (power-of-two) per-group-32 scales, and Hadamard-rotated keys, giving **~2× KV density over fp8**, so more concurrency fits before eviction and decode stays memory-efficient under load. Decode runs on a FlyDSL `D=256` kernel for GQA group sizes **{6, 8, 16}**, with a Triton unified-attention fallback and numerical reference paths. ## Design - New `UltraQuantAttentionImpl`, a standalone subclass of `TurboQuantAttentionImpl`. - `TurboQuantAttentionBackend.get_impl_cls()` dispatches to the UQ impl on the `ultraquant_4bit` cache dtype. - New ops under `vllm/v1/attention/ops/ultraquant/` (FP4/UE8M0 format, Hadamard store, dequant, Triton unified attention, reference) and the FlyDSL D=256 decode kernel/launcher. ## Test Plan - **Unit tests** (`tests/kernels/ultraquant/`): store, dequant, decode, and FlyDSL-vs-reference numerical checks, plus config. - **Serve smokes**: Qwen3.8 (GQA-16, TP=8) and Qwen3.6-27B (GQA-6, TP=2), confirming FlyDSL dispatch (no Triton fallback) and coherent output. - **Accuracy** (KV format is the only variable; sampling fixed): GPQA-Diamond. - **Performance**: SemiAnalysis-style 262K-token agentic replay, throughput/latency and peak KV utilization across concurrency. ## Usage Enable the 4-bit KV cache with `--kv-cache-dtype ultraquant_4bit` (D=256, GQA {6,8,16}): vllm serve /path/to/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-MXFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \ --kv-cache-dtype ultraquant_4bit \ --max-model-len 163840 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --trust-remote-code The 4-bit KV cache composes with MXFP4 weights. Decode auto-dispatches to the FlyDSL D=256 kernel (gfx950), otherwise it falls back to Triton unified attention. All accuracy/perf runs use the sampling settings recommended in the model's Hugging Face card (Qwen3.8: `temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20`). ## Test Results **Accuracy — GPQA-Diamond, mean over multiple seeds.** UltraQuant is at parity with the fp8 (KV8) baseline — in fact marginally ahead on the mean. The decode kernel is numerically exact, so per-seed differences are sampling variance (the arms trade places seed to seed). | Model | UltraQuant 4-bit (mean) | KV8 fp8 (mean) | |---|---|---| | Qwen3.8 | **93.27%** | 92.42% | | Qwen3.6-27B | **86.87%** | 85.61% | **Performance: throughput–latency Pareto (262K-token requests, MI355X):** Qwen3.8 (GQA-16, TP=8). UQ and KV8 track together at low concurrency; UQ pulls ahead from **C=32** onward. KV8 saturates its cache at **C=38 (100%, evicting)** and throughput collapses, while UQ is still at ~44% cache and keeps scaling. | Concurrency | UQ tok/s | KV8 tok/s | Δ | UQ peak KV | KV8 peak KV | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 8 | 193.9 | 199.4 | −2.7% | 8.2% | 14.1% | | 16 | 280.2 | 288.0 | −2.7% | 17.4% | 32.0% | | 32 | 374.0 | 363.1 | +3.0% | 35.1% | 66.3% | | 36 | 398.9 | 299.6 | +33.1% | 39.7% | 82.4% | | 38 | 414.6 | 225.4 | +84.0% | 44.2% | **100.0%** | | 42 | 430.7 | 114.7 | +275% | 45.4% | 99.9% | --- UQ first wins at **C=32 before any eviction** (KV8 only 66% cache), and the gap widens sharply once KV8 hits the eviction wall at C=38. Qwen3.6-27B (GQA-6, TP=2). Same shape; UQ wins even before KV8 evicts at C=42 UQ delivers +9% throughput at lower ITL while KV8 is only ~39% cache. UQ peak KV is ~half of KV8 at every point. | Concurrency | UQ tok/s | KV8 tok/s | Δ | UQ peak KV | KV8 peak KV | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 8 | 268.3 | 271.8 | −1.3% | 4.8% | 8.4% | | 16 | 383.3 | 391.4 | −2.1% | 9.7% | 15.2% | | 32 | 519.9 | 529.5 | −1.8% | 17.6% | 32.1% | | 34 | 545.1 | 537.6 | +1.4% | 19.0% | 31.8% | | 42 | 592.0 | 543.1 | +9.0% | 22.6% | 38.7% | ## Notes - Requires a FlyDSL-capable ROCm build (gfx950) for the D=256 decode kernel; falls back to Triton unified attention otherwise. - Benchmark figures were measured across differing vLLM / AITER / FlyDSL bases, so absolute throughput/latency (and the 8-bit baseline) are indicative rather than bit-identical across environments; the accuracy and relative UQ-vs-KV8 trends are the takeaway. ## References [UltraQuant 4bit KV](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.20474)

commits.pr_title: [ModelRunner V2] Speculative Decoding NGram GPU Implementations
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose


1. Added a new NGram GPU speculator.
The main feature is a new implementation at: `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/ngram/speculator.py`, similiar to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29184.

2. Updated request state storage for NGram GPU.
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py`
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`
This changes how RequestState is initialized so that all_token_ids can stay densely resident on GPU instead of defaulting to UVA when ngram_gpu is active. As discussed in   #29184, the new n-gram speculator repeatedly scans active request token history, doing that from GPU-resident dense storage is much more appropriate than pulling through UVA-backed memory, this is a performance-oriented architectural change supporting the new feature.
The `model_runner.py` also injects req_states into speculators that need direct access to the persistent token store.

3. Added variable-length draft token plumbing
Several files were updated to support draft proposals where different requests may have different numbers of valid draft tokens:
`vllm/v1/outputs.py`
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/utils.py`
`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`
`vllm/v1/engine/core.py`
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`

DraftTokenIds now includes:
`num_valid_draft_tokens: list[int] | None`.
Scheduler logic now truncates speculative tokens based on `num_valid_draft_tokens`.
`EngineCore adds _maybe_update_async_draft_token_ids()` to consume draft metadata from async execution and update scheduler state at the right time.

commits.pr_title: [Misc] Add chat-completion options to gsm8k_eval.py CLI
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Expose chat-completions mode and its request options on the command line of `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`. Today the CLI can only send raw `/v1/completions` requests, so chat-only models (e.g. reasoning models like Qwen3.8 Flash Next) score ~0 when the script is run directly; chat mode exists in `evaluate_gsm8k()` but is reachable only from Python.

## Claims

- New CLI options: `--use-chat-completions`, `--model` (optional), `--reasoning-effort`, `--chat-template-kwargs` (JSON), `--top-p`, `--top-k`; `--max-tokens`, `--temperature`, `--seed` apply in both modes.
- Chat mode needs no `--model`: vLLM's server uses its served model when `model` is omitted. `--model` remains an override (e.g. LoRA names).
- Chat mode uses the server/model default temperature unless `--temperature` is given, and sends no stop strings (the few-shot stop strings only make sense for raw completions; in chat mode they also match reasoning text and truncate it).
- Completions mode is unchanged: same request fields and values as on `main` (temperature 0, same stop strings), and existing Python callers (`test_gsm8k_correctness.py`, offloading / elastic-EP tests) see no behavior change.
- `--save-results` records the effective request parameters under `request_params` (`null` = server default).

## Validation

GPU, 4x GB300, head `999cb73a22` (precompiled wheel at `f98d1fc493`), `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`:
`vllm serve <model> --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code --reasoning-parser qwen3 --max-model-len 16384`, then `python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 <args>` (5-shot, seed 42). `NOTHINK` = `--use-chat-completions --max-tokens 1024 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'`.

| Mode | Args | Questions | Accuracy | Invalid |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| completions (unchanged default) | (none) | 1319 | 0.000 | 1.000 |
| chat, thinking off, server-default sampling | `NOTHINK` | 1319 | 0.957 | 0.000 |
| chat, thinking off, greedy | `NOTHINK --temperature 0` | 1319 | 0.970 | 0.000 |
| chat, thinking off, sampled | `NOTHINK --temperature 0.7 --top-p 0.8 --top-k 20` | 1319 | 0.969 | 0.000 |
| chat, reasoning effort low | `--use-chat-completions --max-tokens 8192 --reasoning-effort low --request-timeout-seconds 900` | 1319 | 0.977 | 0.000 |
| chat, explicit model | `NOTHINK --model <served name> --num-questions 200` | 200 | 0.985 | 0.000 |

The completions row shows the problem this fixes (the model answers raw few-shot prompts with an immediate EOS). Server-default sampling for this checkpoint is temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20 (its `generation_config.json`), hence 0.957 vs. 0.970 greedy. With stop strings sent in chat mode, an earlier revision saw 1% invalid answers in reasoning mode (reasoning containing "Question" was truncated); with none sent, 0%.

CPU: `pre-commit` clean on both files; `--help`; request payloads captured from a fake OpenAI server: the default completions request is identical to `main`'s; chat with no flags sends only `messages`, `max_tokens`, `seed` (no `model`, `temperature`, or `stop`); all chat options are forwarded when given.

## Details

- Reuses the existing `use_chat_completions` path in `evaluate_gsm8k()`; the new keyword arguments are optional and appended, and are sent only when set. `reasoning_effort` / `chat_template_kwargs` without chat mode raise `ValueError` early.
- Answers are extracted from `message.content` only, so reasoning returned separately by a reasoning parser is never scored.
- `evaluate_gsm8k_offline()` is untouched.
- Related: #48253 (closed) added a chat eval mode without reasoning, template-kwargs or sampling options; #52219 (draft) centralizes GSM8K eval definitions and is complementary.
- No new unit test: it would need HTTP mocking; the request-level behavior was checked against a fake server instead (above).

commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Prefer Humming before Marlin backends on SM90
commits.pr_body:
This PR move the priority of Humming before Marlin on SM90.

Humming supports WGMMA on SM90 and delivers significantly better performance than Marlin. In addition, Humming supports more efficient paths such as MXFP4 × FP8 on SM90, so I think it's time to update this.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix mypy safe-super error in EmbeddingGemma2Model
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix the mypy pre-commit failure on `main` introduced by #60254 (`EmbeddingGemma2Model`): `super().__init__()` in a class inheriting `VllmModelForPooling` (a Protocol) trips `[safe-super]` + `[call-arg]`.

## Claims

- Fixes the 2 mypy errors at `vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py:1023` that break the `mypy-3.10`–`mypy-3.13` pre-commit hooks on main.
- No runtime behavior change: the MRO already resolved `super().__init__()` to `nn.Module.__init__`; this makes the call explicit.
- Not a duplicate: checked open PRs for `embedding_gemma2` / `safe-super` / #60254 follow-ups — none address this.

## Validation

```bash
# Fails on main, passes with this change (2 errors -> 0)
mypy --python-version 3.10 vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py
# Also verified: --python-version 3.11, 3.12, 3.13

# The hook as CI runs it, on every file #60254 touched
python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.10 \
  vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_embedding_gemma2.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/config.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py \
  vllm/multimodal/video.py \
  vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_prefill_attention.py \
  tests/models/registry.py

ruff check vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py
ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py
```

All pass. The change is typing-visible only (`super().__init__()` already resolved to `nn.Module.__init__` at runtime), so no model eval was run; happy to run one if reviewers want it.

## Details

Root cause: `VllmModel`/`VllmModelForPooling` are Protocols whose `__init__` requires `vllm_config`. When a class explicitly inherits such a Protocol, mypy treats the protocol's trivial-body `__init__` as the abstract method reachable via `super().__init__()` and rejects the argument-free call. Fix follows the established codebase pattern (`nn.Module.__init__(self)` in `llama_eagle3.py`, `cohere_eagle.py`, `opencua.py`, `qwen3_dflash.py`, `openpangu_mtp.py`).

AI assistance (Kimi Code) was used to prepare this PR; the submitter has reviewed the change.

commits.pr_title: [Metrics] Expose cached prompt tokens by cache tier
commits.pr_body:
## Changes

- Adds `vllm:prompt_tokens_cached_by_source_total{source}` with five values: `device`, `host`, `p2p`, `disk`, `external_unspecified`.
- Counts cache hits at admission. Source counts sum to local and external prefix-cache hits. Existing prompt-token counters are unchanged.
- Records attribution through the existing `PrefixCacheStats` path. Connectors return typed counts through `get_external_cache_hit_sources`. Incorrect totals fall back to `external_unspecified` with a one-time warning.
- Simple offload reports `host` or `disk`. NIXL, Mooncake transfer and MoRIIO report `p2p`. Mooncake Store and uninstrumented connectors report `external_unspecified`. MultiConnector delegates to the selected connector.
- Native offload uses the keys selected for loading. Mixed KV-group dependencies use the outermost required tier, so host + disk reports `disk`. Missing attribution reports `external_unspecified`. Promotion preserves the initiating request's original tier.
- Supports Python and Rust frontends.

Closes vllm-project/vllm#53368.

## Validation

[Passed Run Sweep](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/36272389390): DeepSeek-V4-Pro, one-hour AIPerf AgentX profiles, evaluations disabled. AIPerf scraped Prometheus. JSON/CSV source counts and accounting checks passed.

- B200: [DRAM c8](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/36272389390/artifacts/10917614507), [Simple NVMe c14](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/36272389390/artifacts/10919213254), [native DRAM+NVMe c14](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/36272389390/artifacts/10919342792).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Keep heterogeneous-vocab draft models on Model Runner V1
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Since #43091 (merged 2026-09-28) moved `draft_model` to Model Runner V2, a draft model with `use_heterogeneous_vocab=True` (TLI, #38174) runs on V2 by default. The V2 draft-model speculator (`PlainDraftModelSpeculator`) has no `VocabMapping`, so the target's token ids are fed to the draft model and the draft's token ids are fed back to the target untranslated. Whenever the two vocabularies differ, that indexes past the smaller model's embedding table and the engine dies with a device-side assert. TLI on V2 is still listed as TBD in #47172.

This change reports heterogeneous-vocab drafting as unsupported on V2, so:

- by default the config falls back to Model Runner V1, where TLI is implemented, with the usual warning: `Model Runner V2 does not yet support heterogeneous-vocabulary draft models; using the V1 model runner instead.`
- with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, config validation fails with `Model Runner V2 does not yet support: heterogeneous-vocabulary draft models` instead of crashing later.

## Reproduction (main @ 9e6550bd0, 1x NVIDIA L4 per run, greedy, k=3)

```python
LLM(model=TARGET, speculative_config={
    "method": "draft_model", "model": DRAFT,
    "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "use_heterogeneous_vocab": True})
```

| Target (vocab) | Draft (vocab) | main, default (V2) | main, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` | this PR, default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (151,936) | HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-360M-Instruct (49,152) | crash: `index out of bounds: 0 <= tmp1 < 49152` in the draft's embedding | runs, mean AL 1.88 | falls back to V1, mean AL 1.88 |
| HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct (49,152) | Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (151,936) | crash: `index out of bounds: 0 <= tmp1 < 49152` in the target's embedding | runs, mean AL 2.37, outputs identical to no-spec on 8/8 prompts | falls back to V1, mean AL 2.37 |
| Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct | Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, no TLI | V2, mean AL 3.19 | | unchanged, V2, mean AL 3.19 |

The crash surfaces as `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered` in EngineCore; with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` the assert is the embedding bounds check shown above.

## Not duplicating existing work

Searched open issues and PRs for `use_heterogeneous_vocab`, `heterogeneous vocab`, `TLI`, and `universal draft`. Related open PRs are orthogonal and touch only the V1 path: #51564 (rejects TLI with `use_local_argmax_reduction`), #54780 (tokenizer revisions in the TLI mapping, `vllm/v1/spec_decode/draft_model.py`), and #45018 (SLEM, a different heterogeneous-vocab algorithm, also V1-only). commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Persist FlashInfer autotune cache per rank to fix the rank-0-only cache-hit deadlock
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57423.

`flashinfer_autotune` persists the FlashInfer autotune cache from rank 0 only and, on the next
engine start, broadcasts that file to every rank. FlashInfer keys persisted MoE entries by
`tp_rank` / `ep_rank` (`MoERunner.get_cache_key_extras`), so only rank 0's lookups can hit. A hit
skips the per-tactic reduce of the synchronized tuning pass (`autotuner.py`: "a cache hit skips
that profile's reduce"), so ranks 1..N-1 block in the reduce while rank 0 spins at the trailing
barrier until the 30-minute timeout. Any second engine start that sees the file trips it: a
container restart with the cache directory on a pod-lifetime volume, or a persistent
`VLLM_CACHE_ROOT`.

Fix: each rank saves and loads its own file (`autotune_configs_dp{dp}_rank{r}.json`), and ranks
load only when every rank has a file, decided by one `all_gather_object` over the CPU group. That
gather replaces the previous broadcast and barrier at the same spot, so no collective is added.
Old single-file caches are ignored by name and re-primed on the next start.

## Field report

Observed on one 8xH100 node (SM90), TP8 + EP8 FP8 MoE model, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-8a728663`
(v0.28.1rc1.dev388), FlashInfer 0.6.18, `$HOME` on a pod-lifetime emptyDir.

- The engine died of an unrelated GPU fault. The kubelet restarted the container in place 18 times
  over 8.5 h. Every restart: weights and KV cache fine, then all 8 ranks log
  `Loaded 42 configs from .../flashinfer_autotune_cache/0.6.18/90a/<hash>/autotune_configs.json`,
  rank 0 logs `Config cache hit for trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1 (runner=MoERunner, source=config file)`
  (and `gemm2`), ranks 1-7 sit in `Tuning trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1: k/21 [30:00<...]`, EngineCore
  logs `No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds` every minute, then
  `torch.distributed.barrier` in `flashinfer_autotune` times out and the API server exits with
  `Engine core initialization failed`. Same signature as the log in #57423.
- During the hang: GPU 0 at 100 % utilization, GPUs 1-7 at 0 %; rank 0's worker at 100 % CPU in
  state R, the other seven sleeping. No other process held GPU 0.
- Mitigation/confirmation: renamed only the `flashinfer_autotune_cache/` directory aside and
  restarted the same container on the same GPUs. Autotune ran for 1 s on all ranks
  (`Saved 42 configs`), engine init took 20 s, READY. 19 identical failures, then one success with
  one variable changed.
- The stale and the fresh cache files hold the same 42 keys and identical `_metadata`; the stale
  one is rank 0's, so its keys only match `ep_rank=0`.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py
```

New test: `_all_ranks_have_file` with world size 1, world size 2 all present, and world size 2
with one rank missing (must not load). CPU-only, no GPU needed.

## Test Result

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (0.14.0) clean on both files.
- The three `_all_ranks_have_file` cases pass when run against the affected 8xH100 pod's Python
  (torch available there).
- The full pytest file was not run locally (no torch on the dev machine); relying on CI for it.
- Live validation of the patched build on the affected deployment: not yet. The failure mode
  itself was confirmed by the cache-removal experiment above.

## Note

This is an alternative to #57579 which ensures all ranks load identical files as the leader.
However, the deadlock leading to vLLM being stuck (and subsequently in a crash-loop) on K8s is
caused by non-leader ranks expecting to see their entries in the cache file, so even if all
ranks load files that are identical, you would still run into this issue.

## AI assistance

The the patch, and the test were drafted with Claude Code and reviewed line by line by the author.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Support EmbeddingGemma2 multimodal pooling architecture
commits.pr_body:
# [Model] Support EmbeddingGemma 2 (Omni-Modal Embeddings)

## Overview

This PR adds support for **EmbeddingGemma 2** (`google/embeddinggemma-2`), Google's bidirectional omni-modal embedding model. EmbeddingGemma 2 maps text, image, audio, video, and interleaved multimodal inputs into a unified 768-dimensional L2-normalized vector space for cross-modal and multi-modal semantic search, retrieval, and classification.

## Claims

- **Omni-Modal Embedding Architecture**: Supports single-modal and joint/interleaved inputs across Text, Image, Audio, and Video producing unit-normalized 768-dim embeddings in a single forward pass.
- **Bidirectional Attention & RoPE**: Implements bidirectional attention (`ENCODER_ONLY`) with an inclusive sliding window of 513 tokens (`config.sliding_window + 1`) and 512-dim rotary embeddings (RoPE) across all layers, matching Hugging Face / SentenceTransformers semantics.
- **Upfront Dynamic Modality Loading**: Supports bypassing unused modality encoders at engine startup via `--limit-mm-per-prompt` (e.g., `image=0,audio=0,video=0`). Omitting vision (167.8M params) and audio (305.6M params) loads a lightweight 271.0M param text-only model (~517 MiB VRAM), saving up to 64% VRAM with zero post-load deletion.
- **Dedicated Video Sampling Backend**: Adds `EmbeddingGemma2VideoBackend` to `vllm/multimodal/video.py`, providing 1 fps uniform sampling up to 32 frames with duplicate-frame expansion for short clips (< 1s), exactly matching `EmbeddingGemma2VideoProcessor`.
- **Zero Generative Regressions**: Implemented cleanly as a standalone model in `vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py` without mutating existing generative Gemma 4 model classes (`gemma4.py`, `gemma4_mm.py`).
- **Validated Numerical Parity**: Achieves >= 0.999 cosine similarity against Hugging Face / SentenceTransformers across all 16 multimodal evaluation cases (text, image, audio, video, and mixed inputs).

## Validation

### Unit and Parity Tests

All 20 unit and numerical parity tests pass on NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB:

```bash
# Run standalone unit and parity test suite
pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_embedding_gemma2.py -v

# Verify model registry loading
pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k "EmbeddingGemma2"
```

### CLI Serving Examples

```bash
# 1. Full Multimodal Serving (Text + Image + Audio + Video)
vllm serve google/embeddinggemma-2 \
    --runner pooling \
    --max-model-len 8192

# 2. Text-Only Deployment (Lightweight, ~517 MiB VRAM)
vllm serve google/embeddinggemma-2 \
    --runner pooling \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt image=0,audio=0,video=0 \
    --max-model-len 8192

# 3. Vision + Text Deployment (No Audio Tower)
vllm serve google/embeddinggemma-2 \
    --runner pooling \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt audio=0 \
    --max-model-len 8192
```

### Python API Example

```python
from vllm import LLM
from PIL import Image

# Initialize pooling model
llm = LLM(
    model="google/embeddinggemma-2",
    runner="pooling",
    max_model_len=8192,
)

# Text embedding
text_outputs = llm.embed(["Retrieve relevant documents for machine learning research"])
print("Text embedding shape:", len(text_outputs[0].outputs.embedding))  # 768

# Multimodal text + image embedding
image = Image.new("RGB", (224, 224), color=(73, 109, 137))
mm_outputs = llm.embed([{
    "prompt": "What is depicted in this image? <|image|>",
    "multi_modal_data": {"image": image},
}])
print("Multimodal embedding norm:", sum(x**2 for x in mm_outputs[0].outputs.embedding) ** 0.5)  # 1.0
```

### Numerical Parity Test Results

#### 1. Text Embeddings
```text

  Prompt:    "Hello world"
  Embedding: [-0.0598, +0.0352, +0.0593, -0.0393, -0.0352, ... +0.0396] (dim=768)
  Norm:      1.0000 (unit L2 norm)
✅ PASSED: Shape (768,) and unit norm

TEST: Text Semantic Similarity
  Cosine Sim (A vs B): 0.8914  [Semantically similar: high]
  Cosine Sim (A vs C): 0.6065  [Different topic: low]
✅ PASSED: Similar > dissimilar (0.8914 > 0.6065)

TEST: Batch vs Individual Consistency
  Min Cosine Similarity: 0.999967
✅ PASSED: Batch matches individual encodings (cosine sim > 0.9999)
```

#### 2. Image Embeddings
```text
TEST: Image Embedding (Shape & Norm)
  Norm:      1.0000 (unit L2-normalized)
✅ PASSED: Valid 768-dim image embedding

TEST: Image Discrimination
  Cosine Sim: 0.6324  [Distinct images]
✅ PASSED: Different images have distinct embeddings (0.6324 < 0.99)

TEST: Text + Image Joint Embedding
  Norm:      1.0000
✅ PASSED: Valid joint text+image embedding
```

#### 3. Audio Embeddings
```text
TEST: Audio Embedding (Shape & Norm)
  Norm:      1.0000 (unit L2-normalized)
✅ PASSED: Valid 768-dim audio embedding

TEST: Audio Discrimination
  Cosine Sim: 0.7116  [Distinct audio signals]
✅ PASSED: Different audio inputs have distinct embeddings (0.7116 < 0.99)

TEST: Text + Audio Joint Embedding
  Norm:      1.0000
✅ PASSED: Valid joint text+audio embedding
```

#### 4. Video Embeddings
```text
TEST: Video Embedding (Shape & Norm)
  Video Clip: synthetic_clip.mp4 (4.0s clip -> 4 sampled frames at fps=1)
  Norm:       1.0000 (unit L2-normalized)
✅ PASSED: Valid 768-dim video embedding

TEST: Text + Video Joint Embedding
  Text:       "A video clip showing conveyor belt operations"
  Norm:       1.0000
✅ PASSED: Valid joint text+video embedding

TEST: Video File Loader Input (MediaConnector / VideoMediaIO)
  Video File: file://synthetic_clip.mp4 (32 sampled frames, 3906 tokens)
  Norm:       1.0000
✅ PASSED: Valid video embedding via MediaConnector file loader
```

#### 5. HuggingFace / SentenceTransformer vs vLLM Parity (16/16 Passed)
```text

Single image                   | 0.9991   | 1.0000    | 260     | 260      | 0.999985    | PASS

Prompt + Image                 | 1.0016   | 1.0000    | 267     | 267      | 0.999944    | PASS

Audio                          | 1.0023   | 1.0000    | 22      | 22       | 0.999933    | PASS

Video (frames + metadata)      | 1.0027   | 1.0000    | 368     | 368      | 0.999825    | PASS
Video (file loader)            | 1.0001   | 1.0000    | 3906    | 3906     | 0.999931    | PASS
Text + Image + Audio           | 1.0002   | 1.0000    | 284     | 284      | 0.999907    | PASS
=========================================================================================================
ALL 16 TEST CASES PASSED (token parity + cosine similarity >= 0.999)
```

## Details

### Architecture & Key Components

1. **Standalone Model Architecture (`vllm/model_executor/models/embedding_gemma2.py`)**:
   - `EmbeddingGemma2Model`: Inherits from `nn.Module`, `SupportsMultiModal`, and `VllmModelForPooling`. Integrates vision and audio modality encoders via `_mark_tower_model`, language model backbone (`EmbeddingGemma2TextModel`), and a `DispatchPooler.for_embedding` pooling head with `MEAN` pooling and L2 normalization.
   - `EmbeddingGemma2Attention`: Implements bidirectional attention across all layers using `ENCODER_ONLY` attention. For sliding-window layers, sets sliding window size to `config.sliding_window + 1` (513) to reconcile Hugging Face's `|q - k| <= W` condition with vLLM's `|q - k| < W` encoder attention kernel. Applies full 512-dim RoPE on global attention layers.
   - `EmbeddingGemma2TextPLE` & `EmbeddingGemma2PLEBlock`: Per-layer embedding projections matching the checkpoint weight schema.

2. **Multimodal Processing & Tokenization**:
   - `EmbeddingGemma2ProcessingInfo`: Retains standard `<bos>` and `<eos>` special tokens without applying chat templates, matching SentenceTransformers.
   - `EmbeddingGemma2MultiModalProcessor`: Dynamically budgets soft tokens (`max_soft_tokens=140` per video frame) and suppresses unconditional timestamp prefixing (`exclude_timestamps=True`). Safely masks multimodal placeholder tokens exceeding `vocab_size` before embedding lookups.

3. **Video Backend (`vllm/multimodal/video.py`)**:
   - Registers `EmbeddingGemma2VideoBackend` in `VIDEO_LOADER_REGISTRY` (`embedding_gemma2`).
   - Implements frame index computation mirroring `EmbeddingGemma2VideoProcessor.sample_frames`, with support for uniform overflow capping at 32 frames and duplicate frame expansion for short clips (< 1s).

4. **Configuration & Attention Capping (`vllm/model_executor/models/config.py`, `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_prefill_attention.py`)**:
   - `EmbeddingGemma2ModelConfig`: Automatically caps default `max_model_len` to 8192 (down from the 262k theoretical context) and syncs scheduler token limits while respecting explicit user limits.
   - Triton Prefill Attention: Limits block size to 32 for head dimensions >= 512 to avoid shared memory exhaustion during bidirectional prefill attention.

5. **Upfront Dynamic Modality Loading**:
   - Integrated with vLLM's `SupportsMultiModal` lifecycle: when a modality is disabled via `limit_mm_per_prompt` (e.g., `image=0,video=0` or `audio=0`), the corresponding encoder tower is created on `torch.device("meta")` and skipped during weight loading. Only active weights are loaded into VRAM.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Integer token IDs for generate output logprobs (GenerateLogProbs)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57574
Fixes #59241

Implements the `GenerateLogProbs` shape agreed in #57574. `/inference/v1/generate` is a vLLM-defined token-in/token-out API, but its output logprobs used the OpenAI shape: the generate server has no tokenizer, so it wrote every token as a `"token_id:N"` placeholder string that derender parsed back out, and the two frontends disagreed on `bytes` (Python left it unset, the Rust frontend set it to the UTF-8 bytes of the placeholder itself).

Scope is exactly the split @hickeyma described in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57574#issuecomment-5745092183: this PR is `content` only. #57442 stacks `GenerateLogProbs.sampled` on top afterwards.

## Shape

```python
class GenerateLogProb(BaseModel):
    token_id: int
    logprob: float
    rank: int | None = None

class GenerateLogProbsContent(GenerateLogProb):
    top_logprobs: list[GenerateLogProb] = []

class GenerateLogProbs(BaseModel):
    content: list[GenerateLogProbsContent] | None = None
```

- `top_logprobs` is a **list**, not a dict: JSON turns dict keys into strings and the order would be implicit. It keeps the engine's order: the sampled token first, then the remaining candidates in rank order. With non-greedy sampling the sampled token can be outside the top k (e.g. ranks `[5, 1, 2]`); it then takes one of the k slots and rank k is left out, as on the OpenAI endpoints and the main engine path.
- `rank` is **kept**: the engine already computes it and the Rust frontend's gRPC `CandidateTokenInfo` carries it. It was being dropped on the floor before.
- No `bytes`, no string `token`.
- `logprob` is required, as in #57574 and the Rust frontend. When the sampled token is absent from the engine's top-k map the server passes `-9999.0` explicitly, the value the OpenAI shapes already put on the wire for that case, so it is unchanged.

## What changed

- **Python generate server** (`scale_out/token_in_token_out`): `_create_tokens_logprobs` builds the new type; `GenerateResponseChoice.logprobs` and `GenerateResponseStreamChoice.logprobs` are `GenerateLogProbs | None`, streaming and non-streaming.
- **Rust frontend** (`routes/inference/generate`): same field swap, `position_to_generate_logprobs_content` emits ids + rank instead of `format_token_id`.
- **Derender**: `_resolve_logprobs` converts `GenerateLogProbs` → `ChatCompletionLogProbs`, filling `token`/`bytes` from the tokenizer, and `_convert_chat_logprobs_to_completion_logprobs` then produces `CompletionLogProbs` as before. The U+FFFD byte-fallback correction (`_correct_decoded_token`) is untouched — it needs the preceding sampled token ids as context, and the integer shape now carries those directly instead of reconstructing them from placeholder strings.
- **Placeholder layer deleted from the generate path**: `_parse_token_id_placeholder` and `resolve_token_id_placeholder` are gone; the id-taking core is now `decode_token_id` in `entrypoints/generate/base/serving.py`.
- **Out of scope, unchanged**: `prompt_logprobs` (already integer-keyed) and `return_tokens_as_token_ids` on `/v1/chat/completions` / `/v1/completions`, which is a user-facing OpenAI option that uses `token_id:N` on purpose.

## Release note

> **Breaking:** output logprobs on `/inference/v1/generate` are now `GenerateLogProbs` with integer `token_id` instead of `ChatCompletionLogProbs` with `"token_id:N"` placeholder strings, in both the Python and Rust frontends, streaming and non-streaming. `rank` is now reported and `bytes` is gone. Clients reading only `content[i].logprob` are unaffected; clients that parsed the placeholder should read `content[i].token_id`. Derender output (`/v1/chat/completions/derender`, `/v1/completions/derender`) is unchanged. `return_tokens_as_token_ids` on the OpenAI endpoints is unchanged.

Documented in `docs/serving/online_serving/renderer.md` (new "Generate Output Logprobs" section, with the breaking-change note) and `derenderer.md`.

## Test Plan

- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_generate_logprobs_conversion.py` (new): unit tests over `_resolve_logprobs` with a stub tokenizer — decoding + bytes + rank-order preservation, the U+FFFD byte-fallback path where the second half of a two-byte character is only decodable with the preceding sampled id as context, and `content=None`.
- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_tokens_logprobs.py`: sampled entry carries `token_id`/`rank`, per-candidate ids, `logprobs=0` still emits the sampled token, sampled token missing from the top-k map keeps the `-9999.0` sentinel.
- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py`, `test_derender_parity.py`: derender chat/completion logprob tests and the coupled-vs-derender parity test now feed the generate-shaped payload; parity assertions on `token`/`bytes` are unchanged.
- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py`, `test_serving_tokens.py`: streaming chunks and the sampling-mask test read `token_id`.
- Rust: `routes::tests::non_stream_raw_generate_returns_token_output_envelope` and `stream_raw_generate_returns_sse_chunks_and_usage` assert integer `token_id` + `rank` and a null `token`/`bytes` on the wire.

## Test Result

Rust, locally:

```
cargo check -p vllm-server --tests          # clean
cargo test -p vllm-server raw_generate      # 9 passed; 0 failed
```

The two updated assertions run through the mock engine and confirm the wire shape end to end (`"token_id": 33, "rank": 1`, `token`/`bytes` absent), streaming and non-streaming.

Python, locally (CPU-only box, no GPU):

```
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_generate_logprobs_conversion.py \
       tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_tokens_logprobs.py
7 passed
```

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on every touched file.

Caveat on the local Python run: the box has no GPU, so the interpreter is a vLLM 0.29.0 install with this branch's source on `PYTHONPATH`. That is enough for the pure-Python paths above, but the server-backed entrypoints tests do not run in it. `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py` fails there — identically (29 failed, 1 passed) on unmodified `main` in the same setup, so those failures are the environment, not this change. CI is still the first real execution of the server-backed tests; happy to fix up promptly if anything falls over.

## Essential Elements

- [x] Purpose, shape and scope stated above
- [x] Unit tests for the new conversion, updated tests for every touched path
- [x] Docs and release note

commits.pr_title: [Perf][HiSparse] Cache per-request residency instead of rescanning every page each step
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

HiSparse decode is CPU-bound on main because of one scheduler-side scan. Every step, `HiSparseCoordinator.all_context_pages_resident` walks every page of every scheduled request in every resident group (one group per layer), only to decide whether prefill can skip host staging. That is O(requests × context pages × layers) Python per step, even for pure-decode batches.

The scan arrived in c4b9b7deac ("bypass host resolution for resident decode"), after the GLM-5.3 results in #53781 were measured, and shipped with 3/N. This PR caches the requests whose resident pages are all non-null. A request is scanned once. Pages become null only at admission or host import, before the first scan, or when the pool reuses an unpinned page (`_lose_page`), so those paths plus `free` drop the cache entry. The per-step check is O(requests).

HiSparse-only change (`vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py`). Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this scan.

## Results

GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on B200, fp8 KV, block 64, random prompts, 1k output tokens. Each point is one run, main vs. this PR back to back on the same node and config. The gain tracks how much resident context the scan walks per step relative to GPU step time: it's largest when every page is GPU-resident and contexts are long. It disappears at low concurrency, and in the host-offload regime, where the old scan already exited at the first host page.

| TP | input | concurrency | peak KV | main tok/s | this PR tok/s | Δ | mean TPOT main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 16k | 64 | 61% | 764 | 1209 | **+58%** | 73.3 → 42.0 ms |
| 4 | 16k | 40 | 76% | 809 | 906 | **+12.0%** | 40.9 → 35.7 ms |
| 4 | 4k | 160 | 89% | 2470 | 2583 | +4.6% | 57.7 → 54.8 ms |
| 4 | 4k | 128 | 70% | 2777 | 2882 | +3.8% | 40.1 → 38.3 ms |
| 4 | 8k | 64 | 64% | 1510 | 1551 | +2.7% | 35.8 → 34.7 ms |
| 4 | 16k | 24 | 46% | 744 | 760 | +2.2% | 26.5 → 25.8 ms |

For reference, the TP8 16k c=64 config without HiSparse gives 1302 tok/s and 39.2 ms TPOT. Single-run differences under ~3% are within noise.

```bash
# TP8: host_pool_gib 128; TP4: -tp 4 and host_pool_gib 64 (the host pool lives in /dev/shm)
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --max-model-len <input+2048> --max-num-seqs 256 \
```

commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Layer re-quantization for linear layers through online quantization API (MXFP8 -> FP8 PTPC showcase)
commits.pr_body:
Detailed RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59062

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Purpose

This PR allows re-quantizing linear layers to a different precision using online quantization API, as long as the `dequantize_weight` method for relevant `LinearMethodBase` subclass is implemented.

Similar features have been requested previously in specialized cases:
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48427
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51274

and this feature exists on sglang side https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28291 / https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29328.

Addresses the third item of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52167. This PR is adapted from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48427, co-authored by @tanpinsiang.

This change lets `--quantization-config.linear fp8_per_channel` convert selected serialized ModelOpt MXFP8 linears to FP8 PTPC at load time.

The original checkpoint quantization config remains responsible for unselected linears and MoE.

The composition is handled by the existing `resolve_quant_method`, so model implementations continue to receive their original checkpoint quantization config type.

Quantization methods expose an optional `dequantize_weight` method, that:

- raises `NotImplementedError` by default, or
- dequantizes the quant method weights if implemented.

This draft implements it only for `ModelOptMxFp8LinearMethod`.

Such `dequantize_weight` methods implementation can be shared across model producers (quark, modelopt, compressed-tensors, etc.) based on weight quant key, no model producer-specific code should be required.

## Test Plan

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build] Warm the DP engines before measuring load balance in test_load
commits.pr_body:
## The failure

`test_load` in `tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py` flakes in the `Distributed DP Basic` group, command:
https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13954

```
FAILED v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py::test_load[False-mp-RequestOutputKind.DELTA-hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM]

AssertionError: requests are imbalanced:
  {0: SimpleStatsLogger(init_count=1, finished_req_count=68),
   1: SimpleStatsLogger(init_count=1, finished_req_count=32)}
  assert 32 > (100 // (2 + 1))
```

Both failing parametrizations are the dense model with `async_scheduling=False`, giving 68/32 and 69/31. The threshold is 34, so they miss it by two requests. The MoE parametrizations and the sharded commands in the same group pass.

It is intermittent rather than broken, and it needs the agent to be under load: squeezed onto 12 cores with 20 competing processes it reproduces at 1 failure in 10 runs locally, and idle it does not reproduce at all.

## What causes it

Nothing runs the model between the KV cache being allocated and the first request. Memory profiling does run it, but with attention skipped, and `enforce_eager` skips the capture that would otherwise warm it afterwards. So the first request an engine serves carries the whole one-off setup, about 330 ms, all of it inside the worker's `execute_model`.

With data parallel each engine pays that on its own. While an engine is inside it, the requests already routed to it sit unread in its input socket and its published counts still say it is idle, so the balancer sends the rest of the burst to its peer. The engine then finishes almost exactly the backlog that piled up while it waited, which is where the 32 comes from.

The balancer is not at fault. Withholding work from an engine that is not consuming any is what it is supposed to do.

## How I found it

I reproduced it first, by squeezing the whole test onto 12 cores with 20 competing processes on the same cores, which is the shape of the CI pod. That gives the CI splits exactly, down to 27/73.

Then I timed the busy loop in phases. The wait for the first request is symmetric between engines to within 10 ms, and all of the difference sits in the first step. Inside that step, `schedule`, sampling and output handling are at zero and the entire cost is in `future.result()`, so it is the forward pass and nothing around it. In the failing runs the two engines were 490 ms apart there, against 8 ms when idle, and the engine that waited longer was the one that came up short.

Running the same configuration with cuda graphs instead of eager drops that first step from 346 ms to 4 ms and no backlog builds at all, which confirms where the cost comes from.

## The fix

Give every engine one token before the burst that gets measured, and clear the counts it produced. The assertion and the 100 requests it is made of are untouched.

## Validation

Under the same 12 cores and 20 competitors:

| Runs | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | 1 failed, worst split 32/68 | **10 passed**, worst split 39/61 |

Per-run smallest engine count, threshold 34:

```
before:  49  32  49  47  39  42  43  35  48  50     min 32, sd 6.4
after:   48  44  45  39  45  49  39  49  43  41     min 39, sd 3.8
```

The two series were taken at different times, so the spread matters more than the average: the after series ran on a busier box and still kept every run clear of the threshold.

Whole file, every parametrization, unthrottled:

```
23 passed, 8 deselected in 499.73s
```

`test_load` splits across its eight parametrizations: 49/51, 51/49, 50/50, 49/51, 49/51, 50/50, 52/48, 50/50.

Cost: about 4 seconds per parametrization, 64.9 s against 61.1 s averaged over the throttled runs above.

## Details

It flakes rather than fails because the setup has to be both slow and unequal between the engines, and under CPU pressure it is only sometimes either. That is also why only the dense model is affected: MoE engines step in lockstep, so they pay the setup together and never diverge, and across 10 measured rounds the MoE case never left 48/52.

#59623 was my earlier attempt at this, relaxing the bound when the engines measure as unequally fast. That assumes the assertion is wrong, and the cause says otherwise, so it is closed in favour of this.

The same gap costs real latency outside the test: the first request under `enforce_eager` takes 0.31 s instead of 0.04 s. Warming the model in eager mode fixes that too, but it changes behaviour for every eager start, so it belongs in its own change.
